sections.title: Walkthrough
items: You enter the instance and run through a short hallway to where Perpetua looms over you. The raid takes place for the most part in one large area.
You will fight 2 waves of adds, before a cutscene introduces the first boss encounter.
Overarching mechanics in all boss fights (while Perpetua is big):

1. Giant Perpetua's Eyebeam - Perpetua may point at the bottom left or bottom right of the room before spawning a large Source Beam and moving it across the room. This must be avoided or it will do heavy damage and probably KO in elite. For best practice try not to stand at a beam spawn point (the bottom left/right of the room) at all times during the fight and always have situational awareness of Perpetua and what is happening around you, especially in elite plus. (This may sometimes be credited in the combat log as Divine Source Eyebeam)
2. Planet Strike - Perpetua may spawn several meteors on the group - this is indicated by a large pink AOE. Players should move away from this or it will do heavy damage or probably KO in elite.

3. Source Eruption - Perpetua may make the ground light in some areas*. This should be avoided as it will spawn a source orbital attack in the area of effect. If players are directly affected by this it will do heavy damage or probably KO in the elite version. (Players usually refer to these as 'cracks' due to the design of the AOE)

*Note: Be careful if you use a Supply Drop while having a levelled Philosopher's Stone artifact equipped, as the animation from the artifact proc may limit visibility of Source Eruption AOEs as they appear.

sections.title: First boss: Source Titans: Kerbak, Jakkec, Theon and Proma
items: Recommended roles for regular: 1 tank, 1 controller, 1 heal, 5 DPS Recommended roles for elite: 2 tanks, 1 controller, 1-2 heals (1 preferably), 3-4 DPS Recommended roles for elite plus: 4 tanks, 1 controller, 1 heal, 2 DPS
On PS, Hold Square to lunge
On PS, Hold R1 to block
A fairly straight forward boss encounter in regular, and somewhat challenging but doable in Elite and Elite Plus.
Mechanics:
(Remember the overarching Perpetua AOE mechanics are present in this fight)

1. After a time adds will spawn. Be especially careful of the Fearseeker, as this may do a reflect skull ability. Be also careful of the Skullcrasher adds, as they may charge. In elite if they charge a player/s it is probably going to KO a non-tank player/s on impact if not evaded. If these adds aren't defeated then more shouldn't spawn, so as long as players can mind mechanics like charge/reflect then they can just focus on the Source Titan sub bosses.

2. Source Eyebeam: All of the Source Titan bosses may have a chance of individually pointing at a particular player while having a skull icon above their head. They will then fire a Source beam at that player. This should be blocked or evaded or it will do big damage. Other players should also avoid any AOEs left behind by this.

3. Frost Blast - Jakkec/Proma/sometimes Kerbak may do a skull icon above their head before doing a frost cone attack. Players should not be in front of this as it will do big damage, however this can be countered if a player lunges the boss when this occurs. This may sometimes be displayed as Ice Spray in the combat log.

4. Shamed Ascension - Proma/Kerbak (after losing some health) will look at a player with a skull icon above their head, and after a delay they will fire a light beam at that player, dealing damage and stunning the affected player in the air. When the affected player breaks out of the stun they will do damage to nearby players. This can do moderate damage or more if other players are close by. In Elite Plus this will KO if the player doesn't block - make sure also when you breakout that other players aren't close by (or are blocking) or they will likely take large damage or be KO'd.

5. Eternal Anguish - Proma may do a skull icon while shaking her fist. In elite, players should block when this occurs as it is followed by her Eternal Anguish AOE ability. This can do major damage or can KO players who aren't blocking. There is usually around 3 ticks of damage while this attack occurs, however it is only the initial stomp/tick of damage which should be blocked. Depending on the group's shield rotations/gear it is possible to survive without blocking in regular/elite.. NOTE: Depending on the damage of the group towards Proma it is possible for Proma to do this ability 1-4 times in succession, so prepare accordingly - block the initial stomp and the heal should heal the group where possible.

6. Theon may charge the group on occasion, this is indicated by a skull icon. This does moderate damage and some knock back. He may then stomp the ground ( Melee Stomp). It is best practice to avoid Theon while he charges or does this. Kerbak may also charge the group but less often.

7. Demoralize - Jakkec may spawn a golden AOE field, this does moderate damage over time if players are stood in it. It will also ground and slow movement of players that are stood in it. This is mostly likely to spawn on a player in mid or close range, so ensure that you are max range from Jakkec especially if you are a non-tank role.

NOTE: When you defeat a Source Titan sub boss (Kerbak/Jakkec/Theon/Proma) they will have a cog (with a timer) which you have to interact with. If you for some reason don't activate the cog before its timer runs out the sub boss will respawn again at approximately 45% health. Anyone in the group can do this but it is preferred for a controller or second tank to activate the cog while the heal is healing the group and the DPS are burning the next sub boss or any adds that might be of risk to the group. Failing to do this for Proma may jeopardise the Proma's Anguish feat if you are defeating Proma first, so don't forget to do this.
Differences/considerations in Elite Plus:
For more information, please see the Advanced Walkthrough.

sections.title: Second boss: Dark Knights (Devastator, Dawnbreaker, The Drowned, The Merciless, Red Death, Murder Machine)
items: 4 of these will spawn in total; 2 will be there from the start of the fight and 2 more will spawn later.
In elite, 5 will spawn in total, starting with 3.

Recommended roles for regular: 1 tank, 1 controller, 1 heal, 5 DPS Recommended roles for elite: 2 tanks, 1 controller, 1-2 heals (1 preferably), 3-4 DPS Recommended roles for elite plus: 4 tanks, 1 heal, 1 controller, 2 DPS
On PS, Hold R1 to block

A mostly straight forward boss fight in the regular version provided players know when to block certain mechanics. Fairly challenging but doable in the elite version. The elite plus version of this boss fight is one of the most difficult boss fights in the entire game.
Mechanics:
(Remember the overarching Perpetua AOE mechanics are present in this fight)
Devastator

1. Breath Attack - Devastator may do a cone AOE attack, this should be avoided - indicated by a red AOE tell. If you are in the area of effect you will take damage over time in all versions of the raid but it shouldn't KO with sufficient heals - even then it is unnecessary damage to take so just avoid it if possible.

2. Spike Wave - Devastator may point at a player while having a skull icon above his head. He will then do his Spike Wave cone attack. This will do heavy damage/KO and knock back if any players in front of him don't block or evade this mechanic.

3. Sometimes if a player is close enough Devastator will point at a player while having a skull icon above his head. Devastator will then jump over and do a stomp attack. This will KO anyone who is directly affected by this attack, so players should move out of the way. (In elite, the tank should keep Devastator far to the other side of the room so this should be unlikely to happen, however in elite plus this may be a more likely occurrence.)
- In elite plus Devastator may do 2 and 3 back to back. It is unlikely that he will do 2 Spike Waves back to back or jump to a player twice back to back but in any case prepare accordingly.
Dawnbreaker
It is best practice to not be in melee range of Dawnbreaker, due to some of his skulls including Mangle or Outrage. These can do heavy damage or KO if the player is too close.

Dark Construct Strike - Dawnbreaker may do a skull icon before raising his fist in the air. Orbitals will spawn on all players in range - these should be avoided straight away or they will do heavy damage/KO.
The Drowned
1. Spinning Cyclone - The Drowned may do a skull icon before spinning in the air. Does heavy damage at melee range.
2. The Drowned may do a skull icon before activating a Bubble shield that reflects incoming damage from players. You can currently DPS through this in regular/elite with a competent healer in group.

3. The Drowned (after she has lost some health) will have a skull icon above her head and wait for a short time. Players should block. The Drowned will then do her Call of the Deep attack on all nearby players in range. Any non-tank players that don't block this WILL be KO'd, regular or elite version. Block for a second or two longer after the animation as sometimes a brief damage over time will occur on nearby players after the animation.
The Merciless

Do not use a Supply Drop or Orbital Strike on The Merciless (Elite) under any circumstances. - If you use an Orbital Strike on The Merciless, he will have a skull icon before doing a slam attack. If this isn't blocked any player in the fight will be KO'd from this, and even with a block your health will be low, so with other mechanics it may KO anyway. (Seemingly this isn't the case in Elite Plus, although it may not be working as intended)
Shockwave: The Merciless may do a skull icon before doing a slam cone attack. The tank should ensure that The Merciless isn't facing the rest of the group, and block.

Divine Retribution: The Merciless will do a skull icon, before raising his sword in the air and trying to pull players in. This can be annoying with other AOE mechanics and can lead to tricky RNG situations depending on the timing or positioning of players. This may also deal damage over time to players in close range to The Merciless when this occurs.
Sometimes The Merciless will raise his sword in the air and do a mild Chain Lightning attack, which does mild to moderate damage to all players in range and some crowd control.

The Merciless (after he has lost some health) will spawn unattackable Godkillers, which will follow group members, doing knock back and damage over time ( Spinning Cleave*). These should be avoided if possible. These should disappear after The Merciless is defeated. In Elite Plus as the fight is longer they may disappear then re-appear after a time while The Merciless is active. *(Players may refer to these as 'blades', 'axes', 'spinning axes' or 'spinning blades')
Red Death
Not much to speak of in regular or elite.
1. If you have a red arrow, Red Death will point at you then teleport to you and do moderate melee damage ( Super Speed Multi-Punch). This should be evaded.
2. If you are melee/midrange, sometimes Red Death will hard stun you and you will need to spam a button to break out.
Murder Machine

1. Murder Machine will do a skull icon before shooting projectiles in the direction he is facing ( Bolt Barrage). He will then throw several grenades on the floor in front of him ( Grenade Launcher). If you are in front of him you should go max range and block. If the grenades hit you they will knock back and do significant damage, perhaps KO in elite.

2. Murder Machine will do a skull icon before sitting down and generating a shield. This should be countered/lunged by a player or it will heal MM and then do significant AOE damage to anyone in range. Try not to give Murder Machine immunity when he does this.
3. Sometimes Murder Machine will do a Cable Smash ability which may do damage and knock back anyone in midrange of that ability.
Other mechanics:

Rebuked Isolation and Infectious Ire (below) usually occurs some way into the fight. This is usually from shortly after the last Dark Knight spawns (second additional boss) onwards. In elite plus this also occurs shortly after 2 Destroyer adds spawn along with the last Dark Knight. Rebuked Isolation will occur first and then Infectious Ire after.

sections.title: Second boss: Dark Knights (Devastator, Dawnbreaker, The Drowned, The Merciless, Red Death, Murder Machine) (continued 2)
items: Rebuked Isolation: One player will receive a green stack marker with a timer. As many players as possible should group up on this player in time before the timer ends to mitigate incoming damage (this occurs when the timer runs out), while minding other mechanics. In Elite, if no-one does this this will likely wipe the group.

Infectious Ire: One player will receive a red proximity marker with a timer. This player should go away from the group or it will do significant damage or KO nearby players, if the timer runs out when the affected player is close to other players. (In Elite Plus most/all players in the group will receive this red proximity marker)
Considerations/Differences for Elite Plus:
For more information, please see the Advanced Walkthrough.

sections.title: Third boss: One Who Laughs
items: Recommended role setup (for regular/elite): 1 Tank 1 Heal 1 Controller 5 DPS (some groups may consider 2 heals but 1 is preferred as you will need to damage and KO adds fast). (For Elite Plus): 2 Tank 1-2 Heal 1 Controller 3-4 DPS (Some groups may consider 3 tanks for the add phases instead of a second heal, some groups may be fine with a solo heal and 2 tanks)
A relatively straight forward fight in both regular and elite versions. In Elite Plus somewhat trickier.
Mechanics:
(Remember the overarching Perpetua AOE mechanics are present in this fight)

1. Dark Impale - One Who Laughs may target a player with a white AOE that may hard stun them until they breakout. This does mild to moderate damage over time. If other players are nearby they will also receive this hard stun.

2. Contagious Laughter - One Who Laughs may infect a player with a laughing gas which does some damage and stun. If they are nearby to other players they will also take some damage and be stunned as well.

3. Irrational Dread - One Who Laughs may give players a purple AOE attack, which does damage over time. If other players are close by, the AOE may stun and move players for a time. The stuns may interfere with player's rotations if they don't spread out.

4. As the fight continues, Dark Tentacles will spawn. It is best practice to avoid going near these while minding other mechanics, as if you are caught by a tentacle you will take damage over time until either the group focuses damage on the tentacle to free you, or you are knocked out. NOTE: When the Dark Tentacles spawn, there will be a dark animation tell on where they are going to spawn. Players should stand away from these or if the Dark Tentacle spawns on a player that player will be knocked back and take large damage - most likely a KO in the elite versions.

5. Chain Pull - One Who Laughs will pull all group members to him and hard stun them. Be mindful of breakout timings as this can do damage to nearby players - if too many players breakout at the same time this may lead to KOs especially with other mechanics ongoing. You should try to breakout and roll away before OWL punches the ground ( Ground Slam), although in regular/elite this doesn't do a lot of damage. Ground Slam can knock back players in range and possibly KO players in melee/midrange, especially in elite plus.

6. At approximately 60%/30% of One Who Laugh's health, One Who Laughs will disappear for a time. Darkness AOE pools will spawn, which do damage over time if players are stood on them. These pools spawn adds (Dark Minions) which the tank should aggro and group up. They should be defeated by the DPS as soon as possible while minding the AOE mechanics - they do a lot of damage to the tank if they aren't KO'd quickly. Some of the Dark Minions may use a minor reflect ability.
Differences/Considerations in Elite Plus:
There are more tentacles to deal with, and as such try to KO the tentacles.

One Who Laughs may sometimes teleport and do a pull attack. There will be a tell beforehand where he does a dance and laughs hysterically, so this should be called out and players should block. The pull attack may lead to messy situations with the overarching AOE mechanics or tentacles or both if not blocked. This can also make reviving players tricky in some cases.

Callous Anger: There is a tank swap mechanic, so at least 2 tanks are highly recommended. The One Who Laughs will do a shout emote on one tank (Tank A) and give that tank a red aura. This tank should mitigate any form of incoming damage, and the other tank (Tank B) should aggro One Who Laughs during this time. Later One Who Laughs may do another shout emote at Tank B and then Tank A (with the red aura gone) can aggro One Who Laughs. If a tank takes a lot of damage while having the red aura he may get KO'd and this may lead to a messy situation. Callous Anger may also do raidwide damage to the group when it progresses into further stages. NOTE: This boss encounter is not solo tankable at the current time in elite plus. If one tank continues to get a red aura and is the only tank who has the aggro of One Who Laughs, it may lead to a group wipe. It is imperative that 2 tanks continue to swap aggro of One Who Laughs.

Stunning Force: One Who Laughs will look at a player, slowly raising his hands with a wave motion, and that player will receive a white aura and white arrow. The affected player will be stunned. When that player breaks out they will do a raidwide AOE attack on the group dealing some damage. If players aren't immune or blocking when this breakout occurs they will be knocked back.

sections.title: Last boss: Perpetua
items: Recommended role setup (for regular/elite): 1 Tank 1 Heal 1 Controller 5 DPS. (Some groups may consider 2 healers or 2 tanks but this isn't necessary, however in elite plus 2 tanks is recommended)

A straightforward and somewhat interesting fight if players know where to stand, when to block and to KO Source Titans during add phases, otherwise can be long and potentially tricky. Probably the easiest fight of the raid in the Elite Plus version besides one tricky mechanic.
On PS, Hold R1 to block, hold L1 to target lock
Mechanics:
(The overarching Perpetua AOE mechanics are present during the add phases/Giant Perpetua phases. During small Perpetua phases they are not there.)
Small Perpetua phase (3 in total)

Perpetua's Infinite Source Beam: Perpetua may point at a player while having a skull icon above her head. The player will receive a white arrow followed by a Source Beam attack. This player MUST block (regular, elite or elite plus) for the duration of the Source Beam animation or they will do huge damage to the other group members and most likely cause a group wipe.

Tip: Target lock Perpetua even during the soul phase so you can keep an eye on her when she does this ability (also if you are stood in the area of effect and get hit by this beam and you aren't blocking you can also wipe the group, so try to stay away from the affected player if possible).
Audio tell: "Maybe you should just explode!"
Onscreen text pop-up: "Block to Avoid Overloading when Targeted by Perpetua's Immortal Eyebeams!"

This may also be displayed in the combat log as Immortal Source Eyebeam, especially from the point of view of other players being hit by another group member's beam if that group member is the target.

Perpetua will shield, mitigating damage done to her. She will then transform 3 players and those players will lose their abilities. Those 3 players will have a yellow/orange/red marker above their head respectively, and will then need to interact with 2 souls (3 souls in elite) of the same colour marker in order to regain their abilities again.
There will be onscreen text when this occurs, stating: "Reclaim Fragments of your Soul to Recover your Power!"

Dwarf Planet Strike - During the latter two small Perpetua phases, Perpetua will spawn small red orbital AOEs on all group members several times in succession (2-6 times). These should be avoided or they will do large damage and most likely KO (especially in elite) a non-tank player.

Flame Surge: Perpetua may spawn a pink AOE on herself, attempting to pull players in range towards her, and dealing considerable damage. This may also leave affected players with a damage over time for a short period ( Flame Burst).
Giant Perpetua phase (2 in total at approximately 60%/30% health)

KO 5 Source Titans as soon as possible and collect their rubble to progress the phase. NOTE: Some of these Source Titans may spawn the Demoralize AOE mechanic that Jakkec uses in the first boss encounter. Players should evade these as well as other AOE mechanics. If players stand in the Demoralize AOE they will take moderate damage over time and be grounded, so try to stay out of it if possible.
Be careful of Fearseeker adds or Skullcrusher adds. You can KO Apex Predator adds however more will spawn in their place.
There will also be a number of Source Energy Trail AOEs which will move through the map ("Your existence has been rewoked"). This does damage over time ( Source Scorch) if players stand in it.
Considerations/Differences for Elite Plus:

During the soul phase Perpetua has a shield. In the Elite Plus version this is a reflection mechanic - and extremely deadly for the entire time it is active if anyone does damage to Perpetua while the shield is active. This includes Robot Sidekick, pets, henchmen, combat allies, Grimorum Verum, Quislet, Strategist Card proc, etc. ANY damage being done to Perpetua that is in some way from a player in a group will do large damage to the whole group via the reflection from her shield and will most likely cause a group wipe. As such do not use any pets/henchmen/combat ally etc. and be vigilant with artifact procs especially if you are a Might DPS and especially if you use any damage over time abilities.
The Infectious Ire proximity marker mechanic from the second boss encounter returns in this fight, and again affects most or all players in the group.

Dead Planet: Every so often during the small Perpetua phases, small coloured planet orbs will spawn which players will need to interact with before their timer runs out. If players fail to interact with these in time they may cause debuff mechanics to occur for the group. For example, a heal debuff will mean healing out for the group from the heal will be significantly less for a short time. When activating a coloured orb, that player will get debuffed themselves, rather than a raidwide debuff.
Expand
(Original walkthrough courtesy of TheLQ-DCUO)

sections.title: Trivia
items: During the second boss encounter, you are not allowed to use an Orbital Strike or Supply Drop on The Merciless during the normal or elite versions of the raid, however you can during the elite plus version.
If a player receives the Rebuked Isolation green stack marker, and then is knocked out before the timer runs out on it, the Rebuked Isolation will not impact the group.
This is the first time in DC Universe Online that players get to see the Source Wall, despite references to it through much of the content released previously.

This is likely to be the only released DCUO content to get an in-depth Advanced Walkthrough on its Wiki page, due to how scaled up, long, variable and difficult the second boss encounter is or can be.

The world first legitimate completion of the feat We Owned the Knights (Elite Plus) was completed in early March 2023 (nearly 10 months after release), on US PC/PS server by a mixed group from leagues Allusive, Versed and Ethos.
The world first legitimate completion of the feat Source of Life (Elite Plus) was completed in late January 2023 (over 8 months after release), on US PC/PS server by hero league Versed.
This raid is the conclusion to the ongoing Metal storyline that started with Episode 35: Metal Part I in September 2019.

title: Doom - The One Who Waits
summary: Doom: The One Who Waits is a tier 6 alert in the Legion of Doom episode. It also features an elite version.

sections.title: Overview
items: Justice Token
Doom: The One Who Waits is a tier 6 alert in the Legion of Doom episode. It also features an elite version.
Combat Rating: 333
Event version: Level 12+

sections.title: Story
items: Go to your League Hall with Martian Manhunter to meet Mister Mxyzptlk who has agreed to help you. But something about it feels off...

sections.title: Characters
items: Martian Manhunter
Batman Who Laughs
Murder Machine
Mister Mxyzptlk
Escaped General Kraze

sections.title: Locations
items: League Hall

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Upon arrival at the League Hall, it turns out Murder Machine, who is without a physical body of his own, hijacked the systems, took over the security robots, and frees Batman Who Laughs. The latter has been imprisoned in the League Hall since Call For Allies during House of Legends (Episode), and reveals he has been captured on purpose. You will have to battle Murder Machine and destroy the central computer he is controlling.

sections.title: First boss: Murder Machine
items: The fight will start with a wave of Dark Robin adds, followed by a wave of Armor That Laughs and Heavy Armor That Laughs adds. When defeating these you can interact with the console to start uploading the virus.

There will then be a second wave of Armor That Laughs and Heavy Armor That Laughs adds, and this time you will need to interact with the Heavy Armor That Laughs once they are defeated to progress the phase. You can then interact with the console again to progress to the next phase.

The final phase there will be Murder Machine tentacles that will spawn around the console. These may Swipe and do damage to players if they get too close. Defeat these and interact with their respective timed icons at the same time to be able to access and interact with the console, upload the virus and complete the boss encounter.
Other notes:

In the final phase there will be boom tube AOEs that will spawn (there will be a brief red AOE tell before they spawn). If a player is affected by these they will continually phase up and down through the boom tubes and take damage over time. (In the combat log these are stated as Something)

In the elite version it is best practice to defeat the Murder Machine turrets on either side of the room, as these will deal heavy damage to players ( Light Beam) and may even cause KO's. This is the most likely mechanic (if any) to cause KO's or a wipe in the elite version of this boss encounter. Make sure that the group is focusing on defeating one turret at a time, as if group members go for different turrets they will take full damage from Light Beam and be more likely to be KO'd.

In the elite version Murder Machine drones may spawn in this boss encounter also. When they are defeated they will have a timed icon above their head with a large red AOE tell around them. If they are interacted with the red AOE tell will disappear and nothing will happen. If they aren't interacted in time they will explode, dealing considerable damage and knockback to affected players. (More info needed)

After this, you will explore further into the League Hall and KO more Dark Robins and Armor That Laughs adds. There is an optional add ( Escaped General Kraze for heroes) that players can defeat for a feat.

Once players get to the Power Core of the League Hall, there is a confrontation with the Batman Who Laughs who traps Myxzptlk, and reveals after Alpha Lex Luthor was disgraced at the end of Doom: Umbrax the Ultraviolet, Perpetua is looking to replace him with one of the player's team.

sections.title: Second boss: Batman Who Laughs
items: An interesting but doable boss encounter in the regular version, and rather tricky in the elite version, especially compared with the other two boss encounters in the alert. This is probably one of the more difficult regular elite alert boss encounters by DC Universe Online standards, and requires fairly competent players for best success.
Recommended group setup for elite: 2 DPS, 1 Heal, 1 Tank

In the elite version it is heavily recommended for the tank to have plenty of Chronometric Emitter consumables (from the most recent episode) equipped as they will come in very useful for the add/compound phases.
Mechanics:
Grounding Attack: Batman Who Laughs may do a group wide attack where he may chain to players in range, grounding them and doing moderate/considerable damage.

Chain Pull: Sometimes following Grounding Attack, Batman Who Laughs will hard stun and pull all players towards him, and the players will need to spam a button (Square button on PS) to break out. While doing this Batman Who Laughs will have a red skull icon above his head, before punching the ground ( Ground Slam). This does heavy damage to players in melee/midrange, and knockback to all affected players in range. There is a low chance that this mechanic can be skipped depending on the group damage.

Contagious Laughter: Sometimes a player will get stunned by a red gas and will be hysterically laughing while taking damage over time. If that affected player gets too close to another player they will spread the mechanic to that player also, stunning that player in laughter and giving them a damage over time.

sections.title: Toxin phase
items: Red toxin AOEs ( Environment) will spawn in various areas around the room. These do considerable damage over time if a player is stood in them and affected by them. In the elite version in subsequent phases there will be fewer of these that spawn and they will be more sporadic around the room.

Around the time of these phases, Batman Who Laughs will spawn several adds to assist it in battle, including Dark Robin adds and two add versions of other Dark Knights, such as The Drowned, Dawnbreaker, Red Death and The Merciless. These will spawn around the edges on various sides of the room, so if you are a tank (especially in the elite version), make sure you pull and aggro all adds to you before they start attacking the group. These adds can hit hard especially in the elite version. Try where possible to stun or interrupt adds when they have a red skull icon, especially the Dark Knight adds.

In the elite version, make sure to avoid Dawnbreaker's Dark Construct Strike and Mangle abilities, especially while other mechanics are ongoing as they are likely to do considerable damage if players are affected.

In the elite version, be careful if The Merciless add decides to do its Divine Retribution ability, as this will do damage over time to players close enough, and try to pull players in. If this times with the compound mechanic it may be advisable for the tank to pop group immunity so players don't get pulled out of the toxin AOE at the wrong time.

In the elite version, try if possible to stun The Merciless add's Shockwave slam ability. This slam will do a heavy cone AOE attack in front of it, knocking back players and doing very heavy damage to the affected player. Make sure as the tank that if The Merciless does this that it isn't facing the group, as it will likely KO a non-tank. Even for a tank, you will need considerable shielding, be blocking, and need minimal (if any) damage from other adds or mechanics at the time. This is one of the most likely mechanics in the elite version to cause a group wipe besides the Dark Metal Compound mechanic.

After approximately nine seconds of the red toxin AOEs spawning, there will be onscreen text stating: "Batman Who Laughs is Preparing a Compound!" An objective on the right side of the screen will state: "Touch Toxin to Reduce Compound Damage".

Dark Metal Compound: Batman Who Laughs will prepare a compound, and have a red fire icon with a timer above his head. The timer lasts a few seconds, and once it has run out Batman Who Laughs will use his ability. In the regular version if a player is stood in the red toxin AOE at the time of this impact, they will take moderate damage, however if they are not stood in the red toxin AOE at the time of this impact they will take considerable damage. In the elite version if a player is not stood in the red toxin AOE at this time of this impact they will be KO'd regardless of role.

Do not stand in the red toxin AOE for longer than necessary especially in the elite version, and especially if you are taking damage from other mechanics (ie. the tank). You only need to be affected by this AOE to evade being KO'd by the Dark Metal Compound mechanic.

Finally, when both are defeated, Mister Mxyzptlk is freed but he insists on playing several games with you. In between, you have to defeat several copies of him which is very easy; this is primarily a puzzle boss.

sections.title: Last boss: Mister Mxyzptlk
items: Fairly straightforward boss encounter in both regular and elite versions provided players follow the mechanics.

sections.title: Mxy Says phase:
items: There will be onscreen text stating: "Mxy Wants to Play a New Game"
At the start of the phase there will be a short cutscene, and Mister Mxyzptlk will say to the group: "Oh, this is so much more fun than the 5th Dimension!"

While commencing each emote phase, all players will be hard stunned and grounded, unable to move. When they gain emotes in their loadout there will be onscreen text stating: "Mxy Has Given You New Powers!".

At the start of the boss encounter and in between emote phases there will be a few Mister Mxyzptlk adds that will spawn. Defeat them as soon as possible. In the elite version the tank should aggro and pull them so they don't attack the other group members directly.

sections.title: Regular version
items: Mxyzptlk says: Do the emote he says!
Your abilities will be replaced by 4 emotes.
The correct emote's image will also be displayed above Mxy.

You can also check by opening the actions menu (F1 key by default) and scrolling down to Current Abilities - they are, from 1 to 4, "Laugh!", "Dance!", "Beg!", and "Be Afraid!" (Mxyzptlk calls the last one "Cower").
If you do the wrong one, he will blast you for ~70% of your max health.
There will be 3 emote phases to complete in the regular version.

sections.title: Elite version
items: There will be no onscreen text when Mxyzptlk wants you to do a particular emote, however the correct emote's image will still be displayed above him.
Furthermore your abilities will be replaced by 6 emotes rather than 4.
If you do the wrong emote you will be KO'd regardless of role.
There will be 4 emote phases to complete in the elite version.

sections.title: Dice and turrets phase:
items: There will be onscreen text stating: "Mxy Wants to Play a New Game"
Two giant dice appears. Pick up and drop them to roll them. There will be onscreen text when this occurs stating: "Smash the Dice!".
Add the two numbers up, then destroy the equivalent number of turrets. There are 6 turrets in total.
If you get the number wrong, he will also blast you (the combat log will imply that Mister Mxyzptlk is attacking you directly, and the blast does not have a mechanic name specifically).
In the elite version if you get the number wrong it will likely do very heavy damage or probably KO most or all of the group, resulting in a group wipe.

There will be a few Mister Mxyzptlk adds that will spawn. Defeat them as soon as possible. In the elite version the tank should aggro and pull them so they don't attack the other group members directly.

sections.title: Presents and balls phase:
items: There will be onscreen text stating: "Mxy Wants to Play a New Game"
There will then be onscreen text stating: "Avoid the Bouncy Balls and Destroy Presents to Play Mxy's Game!"

Similar to The Vault, destroy all presents while dodging several 5th Dimensional Bouncy Ball that would damage, ground you and knock you back. If a present isn't destroyed by the time its timer expires, miniature Dark Knight themed adds ( Red Death, The Merciless, The Drowned, Dawnbreaker) will spawn.

There will be a few Mister Mxyzptlk adds that will spawn. Defeat them as soon as possible. In the elite version the tank should aggro and pull them so they don't attack the other group members directly.

It is best practice in the elite version if all players have Brawling as a weapon, have Weapon Mastery unlocked and be using the Shuriken Storm Mastery weapon combo for this phase. It will make destroying the presents significantly easier.

Upon winning all games, Mxyzptlk finally relents and agrees to open a doorway to the Sixth Dimension, from which the Sixth Dimension Superman emerges. Martian Manhunter intends to go and convince the World Forger to aid against Perpetua.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Sixth Dimension Hall of Justice

Upon arrival, Sixth Dimension Superman reveals that the player team does not align with his idea of justice and thus is jailing them for a life sentence. Sixth Dimension Miss Martian reveals she read their minds but decided to help you. Fight your way through jailors - Sixth Dimension Miss Martian confesses that the denizens of the dimensions are not real and more like "blueprints", although Martian Manhunter is happy to consider her family as well - until you face Warden Lois Lane (and her sidekick Jimmy Olsen).
Overarching mechanics for the elite stages of this raid:

Mental Distortion: Martian Manhunter will be active in the fight as a NPC that you can interact with. Random player/s will receive a Mental Distortion aura which deals damage over time. This can be cleansed by interacting with Martian Manhunter. If a player goes near another player while they have this aura they will give this player an aura as well, with the same effects. After a while this aura will disappear. The amount of times you can interact with Martian Manhunter may be more limited in the higher elite stages, so have this in consideration.

sections.title: First boss: Warden Lois Lane
items: The fight will begin with several waves of Jailer adds (usually 4 in the elite versions). The tank/s should pull these together and the group should defeat them as soon as possible. During this initial phase Warden Lois Lane is not active in the boss encounter.

NOTE: The group should be especially careful of the Jailer Sniper add. These may target a random player and give them a rotating blue target icon. The Jailer Sniper will then have a Lethal Attack icon. If the Jailer Sniper isn't stunned, or countered/interrupted with a lunge while they have this icon, they will fire an attack at the targeted player dealing considerable damage. In the elite versions this will likely KO. It is possible to have more than one Jailer Sniper add active in the fight at the same time.

There is a chance that the Jailer adds may cuff and stun or even hard stun a random player or player/s. If this occurs you may need to spam a button to break out (for example the Square button on PS). These may also deal damage over time.
Towards the end of these initial add waves, Warden Lois Lane will join the fight. In the elite versions this is usually towards the end of the fourth wave of adds that spawn.
Mechanics:

Omega Cannon: This targets every player simultaneously with a big red reticle (she calls out to Jimmy to fire the omega cannon) which should be dodged. If this affects players these do heavy damage over time, and will likely KO in the elite versions. In addition, in elite and the elite stages these may spawn in succession 1-4 times, so players will need to be agile and keep avoiding them when the big red reticle appears.
There are several attacks with a Lethal Attack icon that Warden Lois Lane does that can be lunged/countered to interrupt. If these impact the targeted player they can do major damage.
The tank or tank/s need to be competent at keeping the adds that spawn together. If most are defeated once Warden Lois Lane is out more adds will spawn in their place.
Considerations/differences for elite stages:
Consider that while Warden Lois Lane is active in the boss encounter, that overarching mechanics for the raid are active.
Omega Cannons will start earlier in the fight. For example in the Critical elite version they will start during the third wave of Jailer adds.

In the severe/critical versions of the raid (when Warden Lois Lane has taken significant damage) 1-2 players may be teleported to one of the two side rooms. There will be an add in the side room which those players will need to defeat quickly in order to teleport out of the side room and return to the main boss encounter.
Upon her defeat, Sixth Dimension Superman whisks her away.

The raid group will proceed through several corridors and encounter and defeat several more Jailer adds. At the end of these corridors will be another big room, where Sixth Dimension Superman will be awaiting you.

sections.title: Second boss: Sixth Dimension Superman
items: Mechanics:

Super Flare: His most notable attack, in which he flies to the centre of the chamber, and after a brief delay, hits everyone for massive damage, unless you are hiding behind one of the four pillars. However, every time he uses Super Flare, one of the pillars are destroyed until only one remains (sometimes the message appears but the pillar doesn't get destroyed). Super Flare will likely KO in the elite versions if players are affected, unless the players are out of line of sight behind a pillar.
He also has a second lethal attack, a melee slam that deals heavy damage to nearby targets and knocks them back.

Whirling Arms: Sixth Dimension Superman will teleport somewhere in the room (usually near a random player) and raise his hand in the air and wait for a short time. He will then use his arms to create a vortex, dealing damage and push back targets in front of him; vulnerable to interrupt via lunging the boss. In the elite versions this may KO players in range whom are hit directly by this. Ensure that this is safely countered, or that all players are out of range. NOTE: You can counter this while Sixth Dimension Superman has his hand raised during that short period before he uses Whirling Arms.
Focused Blast: A heat vision that deals heavy damage and pushes back a single target.

At approximately 75%/50%/25% health, Sixth Dimension Superman may summon adds to his side. These should be pulled together by the tank/s and KO'd ASAP by the DPS in the group. (More info needed on add types and their abilities)

Sixth Dimension Superman may periodically spawn several doors* to other dimensions across the room. Players should position so that they are not in between two of these doors. Sixth Dimension Superman will then fire a heat vision into one door that will link across between all the doors in the room. Anyone hit by this heat vision will take heavy damage, and most likely be KO'd in the elite versions. (More info needed) *Players may refer to these doors as 'mirrors'
Considerations/differences in the elite stages:
Consider that overarching raid mechanics will be active throughout the boss encounter.
Sixth Dimension Superman may periodically summon a Statue of himself (add) to assist him in the boss encounter (more info needed)

Upon defeat, he turns out to be the World Forger in disguise, much to the shock of Lois - who has endured numerous cycles of their lives being remade. He declares he now knows what perfect world he must make into reality, and is the next boss.
Sixth Dimension Courtyard

The rest of the operation occurs in the Sixth Dimension Courtyard and is considered to be an open world. Whenever you get KO'ed and flee, you will respawn on the north side, next to a convenient vendor to repair your gear, and can rejoin immediately. The boss fights would only reset if every player is simultaneously knocked out.
When you arrive at the Sixth Dimension Courtyard, World Forger awaits you.

sections.title: Third boss: World Forger
items: Mechanics:
Pools of Creation: If a player stands in these they may be turned into a creature for a limited time, and unable to use their loadout during this time.
World Forger also has a hammer special attack (massive continuous damage in a long cone in front of him)

World Forger may sometimes walk towards the anvil and smash his hammer on the anvil. This deals massive raidwide damage (likely KO in the elite versions) unless players are blocking (can be blocked to reduce damage to about 10%). Following this, adds will spawn somewhere in the room, usually either on the top left, top right, bottom left or bottom right of the room. These should be pulled by the tank/s and KO'd ASAP by the DPS in the group. There is a chance that a Jailer Sniper may spawn among these, so make sure these are stunned/countered when they have a lethal attack icon above their head. (More info needed)
Both the mechanics above are called out with text popups. (More info needed on what these are)

World Forger may pick up a giant blue crystal and throw it towards a random player. If the crystal hits a player it will deal mild damage, some knock back, and the affected player will lose significant power. If the crystal hits the outside barrier of the room it may bounce back a little.
(More info needed on cage mechanic)
Considerations/differences for the elite stages:
Consider that overarching raid mechanics will be active throughout the boss encounter.

World Forger's crystal will deal significantly higher damage and may KO if he throws it and it hits a player directly, especially in the severe and critical elite versions. Avoid being hit by this and be mindful that the crystal can bounce off of the outside barrier of the boss encounter.

Upon defeat, the Monitor appears, having recruited the Anti-Monitor, and the World Forger agrees to help. However, the Batman Who Laughs appears and mocks the reunion, saying they forgot someone. Perpetua's voice rings out and convinces Anti-Monitor to turn against the team.

sections.title: Final boss: Anti-Monitor
items: Mechanics:

Do not use orbitals during the final fight against the Anti-Monitor. If you do Anti-Monitor will spawn purple orbital markers on all players, which they will need to avoid immediately. If affected these purple orbital strikes will deal massive damage over time, likely a KO in the elite versions.

The key mechanic is the light blue safe zones - if you are outside of them, your power would all be drained in seconds. They eventually become corrupted, turning purple (can be hard to see as it is the exact same shade as Anti-Monitor's attacks), forcing you to move to new safe zones.
Flame Surge and Flame Burst: Anti-Monitor draws in all targets before blasting them back.

Corruption Beam: Players take damage from any nearby player, making it less ideal to cram into one safe zone. Worth noting that safe zones extend all the way upwards to the ceiling of the area, allowing flyers to be in a safe zone but far enough away from players on the ground (as long as you are not grounded).
Periodically, Qwardian adds will spawn to assist Anti-Monitor. These should be pulled by the tank and KO'd ASAP by the DPS. Consider that later adds may spawn again if they are defeated.
Considerations/differences for the elite stages:
Consider that overarching raid mechanics will be active throughout the boss encounter.

Some groups may consider 2 tanks, with one pulling and keeping aggro of the adds, and the other with the boss. As more adds will only spawn if previous adds have been KO'd, this allows the remainder of the group to focus mostly on Anti-Monitor.

Qwardian Snipers may spawn with the adds in the higher elite stages. These behave similarly to the Jailer Snipers from earlier in the raid, so ensure that these are stunned/countered when they have a lethal attack icon above their heads. Their primary attack will KO the targeted player if it isn't interrupted by a stun/counter. There is a chance more than one of these will be active in the fight at a given time.

Upon his defeat, he states he has already done enough to stall you. World Forger claims he now understand what world he needs to build, but the Monitor informs him that Perpetua and Batman Who Laughs has already remade the world, leading into the events of Dark Knights (Episode).

items: Confront Sinestro and his Ultraviolet Lanterns at the LexCorp moon base before their invasion reaches, and dooms, Earth!

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Fight your way through the Ultraviolet Lantern Corps with John Stewart until you confront Ultraviolet Sinestro inside the base building, who leaves behind a Construct (based on one of the original 6 Mentors) to fight you. Its most notable attack is Ultraviolet Freeze, which freezes one player solid and the other player must use an interrupt attack to stop it. Walking into the ultraviolet forcefields on the side of the room would cause heavy constant damage.

Going back in the open area, you fight Ultraviolet Sinestro himself. His deadliest attack is Ultraviolet Outburst, which causes massive damage to anyone outside John Stewart's force bubble that appears when Sinestro is about to use that attack. Sinestro also summons numerous constructs at once; upon their defeat, they remain on the ground, and when the full wave is defeated, all defeated constructs simultaneously explode.

An image of Perpetua appears and "rewards" Sinestro's doom-bringing by binding him to her throne. Alpha Lex Luthor appears and taunts Sinestro for his failure and only worthy of feeding Perpetua. After fighting through another wing of the moon base, you confront Alpha Lex Luthor. He is fairly simple other than that Source Creations would spawn constantly from the south side of the room. They use Hand Blast and their numbers and damage can rack up very quickly, so it is important to kill them, which is easy since they have low health. There is a health barrel next to the north wall.

Upon Alpha Lex Luthor's defeat, he calls out to Perpetua for aid, but to his chagrin, she proclaims he is not deserving of the Source energy and siphons it off him, reverting him to regular Lex Luthor. Furious, Lex denounces Perpetua and belittles the Monitor's plan to oppose her, stating he will lead himself.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Sinestro's fate would later be revealed during Dark Knights: Return to Earth 3.

Lex Luthor returns after his disappearance at the end of BoP: Fire & Brimstone. After losing his Source energy, his armor returned to a green and purple colour scheme, although it retained its sleeker design. His old, bulkier warsuit can be seen side by side in BoP: Fire & Brimstone, briefly commandeered by Jimmy Olsen. He retains the old suit in most instances, but the new design is retroactively applied to Lex in the base game.
The rocket at Lex's moon base is emblazoned with "SPACELEX", likely an allusion to SpaceX, a real-life space company.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Talk to the scientist and then enter the large free area to start the raid. The Doomsday Plague Probiotic is not a must to use, but will provide additional shielding effects and help the healer to keep the group on their feet.

The raid features just one boss, Doomsday (Metropolis: Ground Zero). Ranged attacks are recommended since his Jackhammer-like attack ( Rage Rumble) is lethal and even good healers might have problems healing through it. If you must do melee damage, roll away when Doomsday starts jackhammering.

From time to time Doomsday will vanish into the air and then several more or less large red crosses will appear on the ground. Avoid those because when Doomsday comes down again, these crosses will be regions of air strikes. Avoid the blue crystals and ground AOEs. Those will also damage you.

From time to time sick civilians will become active near the edges of the area. If Doomsday reaches those, he will grow stronger. Players near the civilians or the controller should go and interact with them to prevent this. Managing to do all civilians - or none - will also get the group a feat.

Once Doomsday is at about half health, he would begin rapidly regenerating any further health lost back up to the threshold. Oracle/Calculator will tell you about the Kryptonite Turrets. Three of those will appear and should be used to fire them as soon as they become active. This needs to be done three times and these turrets will damage Doomsday enough to bring him down finally.

While this raid is possible to do without a tank since Doomsday is quite untankable anyway, going in with a healer is an absolute must. The blue spore cloud surrounding Doomsday does constant damage ticks and will kill the group without Doomsday even interfering. The Doomsday Plague Probiotics can help to lower this damage effect, but a healer is still highly recommended.

sections.title: Trivia
items: There is a glitch that may occur during the raid that causes Doomsday to be invisible after he leaps into the sky and crashes back down. He is still targetable however, and fairly easy to spot due to all player-inflicted effects such as Burning still visible on him.
The Doomsday Raid is the only On Duty instance to be named directly after a character. The map refers to the area as "Metropolis: Ground Zero".
It is also likely the only instance ever to only have a single opponent with it, without any mobs to fight through prior or minions that aid the boss.

At the end of the raid, Green Lantern would encase Doomsday's body in an energy bubble. However, if you are next to the body right after the cutscene ends, the bubble will trap you as well, preventing you from leaving other than warping via the Map.

items: At the end of Earth 3: The Panopticon, the Crime Syndicate of America have located the "Prime" Earth and attempts to conquer it as well. The first boss is Kill Bot 9000 aided by many other drones, and eventually Owlman joins the fight while Johnny Quick starts opening a portal.

Finally, you must fight Ultraman, who is joined by Superwoman and then Owlman (who can revive Ultraman if he is KO'ed). Throughout the fight, Johnny Quick is running in circles in a tube attempting to generate a portal, but he feels something is not right. Upon defeating the evil trinity, Johnny Quick stops, exhausted, failing to create a proper portal but tearing a hole between the universes, and Alexander Luthor heavily states that something terrible is coming. All the assembled heroes and villains from the Prime Earth must escape Earth 3.

sections.title: Additional Lore
items: After defeating Owlman, Superwoman, and Ultraman, you are told to escape Earth 3, but you can talk to Wonder Woman, Alexander Luthor, and The Flash in that order for a line of bonus dialogue. Wonder Woman fears this world is irredeemable, Alexander states his determination in not letting the Crime Syndicate ruin another Earth, and The Flash says like Johnny, he can also feel that something is coming. The heroes of Prime Earth depart after you talk to them, leaving Alexander standing alone in the final room.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Generally if you are in relevancy range of this raid, do not underestimate the adds in the hallways. Those are a serious threat, especially the stronger Enhanced Security Mechs.
In the hallway between the first and the second boss there is a laser barrier going up and down which is lethal. Do not stop there when fighting the adds.

In the hallway between the second and the last boss you can find a console near a door. If you use it, it will open the backdoor of the room where you started and thus a shortcut to the hall of the final fight in case of the group wiping. It is recommended to use it or everybody would have to take the long way around.

sections.title: Johnny Quick
items: Aided by Superman and Wonder Woman, your first opponent is Johnny Quick, who reveals the Crime Syndicate has captured Lex Luthor and is siphoning information from his mind.
There are two notable attacks from the boss in this fight.
a) The mirror images

When Johnny Quick spawns his mirror images, those will explode after their timer runs out. The easiest strategy here is for the group to gather in the center of the hall and block. Quickly kill the mirror image possibly spawned in the center.
b) The energy rope

From time to time Johnny Quick will tie three players together with an rope of energy which pulls those players together. Constantly roll against the direction of the pull since if you bump into the other player(s) you will be dead. The boss needs to be lunged when he starts this attack to avoid it.

sections.title: Owlman
items: The second boss is the Owlman, who has Lex Luthor trapped behind him. There are two mechs at the back that would fire into the arena if not destroyed in time, although it is probably faster to take Owlman down directly. They can either shoot in a straight line with machine guns, or lob a bomb to a spot which creates a field of fire that deals damage over time.

The Owlman fight is all about positioning. Absolutely avoid the pistol (cross) fire from the two Enforcement Mechs and roll out of any fire ground AOE immediately. Most tanks will hold Owlman in the front of the room between the two mechs.

sections.title: Ultraman
items: After Lex is freed, he runs off on his own to confront Ultraman. He throws a kryptonite spear at him but is shocked when it is revealed kryptonite empowers instead of weakens him. Defeat Ultraman to finish the raid.
The final boss fight is full of mechanics you need to be aware of, especially if you are planning to do the elite version of the raid. It is generally a good idea to stay at least in mid-range.

When Ultraman uses his freeze breath to encase you, do not breakout. After it he will immediately use his heat vision to 360 degrees which will kill you if you cannot avoid it. You can also try to jump over it, but the safest strategy if not encased in the ice is to quickly go to either side of the hall where his heat vision cannot reach you. Hiding behind an encased player may also work. This mechanic will happen several times during the fight and it is a good idea to look for downed players in the whole room after it is over.
Ultraman will occasionally lunge a player, which should be answered with a roll. However be aware that he might follow you with a second lunge, so be prepared for a second roll.
The mean thing in this final fight is that the three large statues in the back (Owlman, Ultraman and Superwoman) are attacking the players from time to time to create diversion.
Superwoman Statue

The Superwoman statue will use the Lasso of Submission on one player. If this happens you need to quickly and repeatedly press fire (left mouse button on PC) and you will finally be able to break out.
Owlman Statue
The Owlman statue will send a couple of Gadgets Mines into the room. If you hear their high spin sound immediately roll away, in Elite the mines can kill you.
Ultraman Statue
The Ultraman statue will drop a couple of small red sparks into the room which will cause heavy damage over time if you get caught in their explosion.
(Please note that many of the above mentioned mechanics will do much less harm in the regular version of the raid, but most if not all will be lethal in the Elite version.)

Energy Armor is an Iconic Battle Suit for heroes and villains which is also available in an Elite version.
Consisting of eight pieces, the set is an advanced PvE ( Player versus Environment) gear set inspired by Lanterns and their power constructs.

This set has Item Levels 120, 123 and 126 and is obtained as loot drop from the tier 7 raids Unholy Matrimony (elite) and The Bombshell Paradox as well as the Desecrated Cathedral (elite) alert. A minimum PvE Combat Rating of 113 or above and episodes 15, 16 and 17 are pre-requisite of obtaining this gear.
The costume style is also available as style items named Envisioned Energy from Vending Unit 44 in the Archive of Victory of the House of Legends.

sections.title: Trivia
items: In act 2 for heroes the screen objective speaks of WayneTech Oppressors although the enemies in question are WayneCorp Oppressors.
There is a Briefing in the Alternate Gotham section called What Could Have Been in this operation that gives the Dark Defender hand style.

The Iconic Speed Force Traveler encounter is unique not only in that they are an optional boss, but also that you need to constantly attack them or they will stop attacking, keep moving to the end of the Speed Force and disappear.

During the Speed Force segment, if you take too long the portal to alternate Gotham may not work. In that case, you can warp rally back to the Flash Museum, and use the portal into the Speed Force, which would now go directly to alternate Gotham.

Both versions of the operation for villains and heroes apparently negate each other in the end. As the Heroes must solve the paradox created by the villains, the heroes themselves create a paradox in the end the villains must solve, and again in an endless cycle.; The heroes end up in a Gotham where Lex Luthor found a young Bruce Wayne mourning his just-killed parents and took the boy under his wing as an apprentice, leading him to grow up with Luthor's style of crooked business dealing. The heroes end up going back to that fateful night in Crime Alley and preventing the deaths of Thomas and Martha Wayne.; The villains come to a Gotham where Thomas and Martha Wayne didn't die in Crime Alley and went on to work with their son Bruce to turn Gotham into an idyllic paradise. The villains end up going back to that fateful night in Crime Alley and ensuring the deaths of Thomas and Martha Wayne, which sets up Lex Luthor to take their son Bruce under his wing as a protégé in the art of crooked business dealing.
In the feats section, Family Reunion is currently described as a duo, even though it's an alert.

sections.title: Story
items: With the realization that you were in Kid Flash's nightmare perpetuated by Brainiac, find and confront Brainiac to put an end to this!

sections.title: Characters
items: Flashpoint Cyborg
Kid Flash
Brainiac

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: At the end of FP: Flashtastic Voyage it is revealed Kid Flash is trapped in Brainiac's nightmare world. FP: Flash to the Future opens with Flashpoint Cyborg busting Kid Flash out of his pod in a Brainiac fortress.

After fighting through some mobs, you face the only boss, Brainiac. He has 3 phases (with the same health bar); whenever he loses 1/3 health, there is a brief cutscene and you gain loot. KO'ed players can rejoin as if the next phase is a different boss. However, mobs will remain, and you will be repositioned by the cutscene, so pay extra attention at the transition to avoid being caught unawares. He has these attacks:

Furnace Blast: Brainiac may stomp on the ground, dealing considerable damage to players or pets nearby. He usually does this a few times at the start of each phase after commencing the boss encounter or phase for the first time. In elite or the elite stages any non-tank roles should stay max range of Brainiac when he does this otherwise it will do very heavy damage or likely KO affected players.

Spin Charge - Brainiac spins in place before charging towards the player with the red marker over his/her head. This is usually indicated initially by Brainiac doing a point emote at the targeted player.
Afterburner - After marking the area in red, he blasts a cone in front of him with his exhaust jets, pushing all targets back. This does heavy damage and will KO in the higher elite stages.

Multiplicity Flash - Brainiac creates a brightly flashing golden-purple circular wall around himself (with a red circle indicator warning shortly before). The radius varies with each use. Passing through or touching the wall deals continuous damage.
Multiplicity Singularity - Similar to above, but a beehive-shaped wall instead; this gives no warning but is always small in radius.
Multiplicity Beam - 4 thin orange beams on a horizontal plane, 90 degrees away from each other, that is emitted by Brainiac and extends to the walls of the room.
Electrical Burst - Glowing, pulsing orbs on the ground that damage any nearby players continuously.
The Flash's Energy Root - Jay Garrick, trapped on the ceiling, shoots down bolts of continuous lightning that damages targets that come into contact.

Brainiac can summon two noninteractive images of himself at one wall and teleport himself between them. After briefly marking the area in red, all three bombard a broad line directly in front of them across the whole arena (ignores Shield Powers). If this hits a player it deals heavy damage (it is implied this mechanic is being dealt by Brainiac directly in the combat log; this mechanic does not have a name specifically)
Pull - Starting in phase 2, he additionally gains the ability to pull in all nearby targets, damaging them.

The Flash's Voltaic Bolt - Jay Garrick shoots beams that creates spots of wild electricity on the ground that damages and stuns any target nearby (warned by a red targeting reticle shortly beforehand).

Brainiac may do a Pulse Beam attack on a random player. This does heavy damage over time and the player may need to block - heals and shields will also help. In the harder elite stages this will probably KO so it may be advised for all players to run Amazonium Deflection in their loadout to mitigate incoming damage, and use this only when Brainiac is going to use Pulse Beam on you.

Adds will spawn shortly after the phase starts, the tank should pull these and stay to the top right of the room. The adds do not need to be KO'd, unless for feats. The tank should be mindful at all times and be ready in case Brainiac targets the tank with Spin Charge. It may be advisable in the harder elite stages to run with 2 tanks if incoming damage is too much for the 1 tank with the adds.
Brainiac may occasionally do a cone attack with several fireballs. These can do major damage in regular elite but can KO on impact in the higher elite stages.
Around the edge of the room turrets may spawn and shoot projectiles. These can do damage, heavy damage in the harder elite stages.
Multiple Digitized Jay Garricks are summoned to fight you.
Considerations/differences for the harder elite stages:

From stage 2 and higher, Brainiac Neurocrawlers will spawn, these having a timer above their heads. They will walk across the map towards a random player. When the timer runs out these adds will explode ( Charged Blast), doing some knock back and considerable damage within the area of effect. Players should evade these. In the harder elite stages these are more recurrent, the range of the AOE is greater, and the explosion is likely to KO especially for DPS, controllers or healers.

In the harder elite stages, it is possible during Brainiac's invulnerable/bombard phase with the 3 red AOEs for him to immediately use Spin Charge on a targeted player after. This doesn't always occur but prepare accordingly as if he will actually charge/impact for real, as sometimes this can happen.

After defeating Brainiac, Jay Garrick is freed. Together with Kid Flash and The Flash, they run off in an attempt to fix the timeline. Flashpoint Cyborg expresses his hope that it worked. (This is not a cutscene and can be missed if you leave right after getting loot.)

sections.title: Locations

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: You start off on a street in Nightmare Central City, where you and your raid group fight through a few hallways of nightmare gorilla adds. Eventually you encounter a nightmare version of Gorilla Grodd.

sections.title: First boss: Gorilla Grodd
items: A very straightforward boss encounter in the regular version. Can be tricky in the elite version if the group doesn't adhere to the mechanics or KO Gorilla Specialist adds before they have a chance to form change a player/s into a gorilla to adhere to said mechanics.
Mechanics:

sections.title: Gorilla Specialist add mechanic/considerations:
items: One of the key mechanics of this fight is that Gorilla Specialists will spawn in the fight alongside other adds.
The other adds can be defeated but the Specialists are crucial as they may transform a player in range into a gorilla.

Being transformed into a gorilla allows you access to teleport onto one of the ships above the boss room to turn off various mechanics, such as knock back bombs or AOEs (including Gorilla Eradication Platform). This is more important to note in the elite version, unless you are trying to obtain certain feats.

- While in the gorilla form, you can do large damage to other gorilla adds with some of your abilities. it is helpful in elite to use this to your advantage so the group doesn't become overwhelmed with adds or damage from adds. - Carefully KO adds on the ship you teleport to, however try not to die on the ship as it is very unlikely you will be revived unless another player is also transformed into a gorilla and goes to the same ship as you.
The gorilla specialist mechanic should be taken seriously in the elite version otherwise the elite version of this fight may become tricky for the group. Otherwise a straightforward fight.

It is best practice especially for the elite version to avoid KO'ing Gorilla Specialists where possible, as if no-one is being transformed into a Gorilla due to Gorilla Specialists being KO'd too fast then the fight becomes more chaotic due to more adds and AOEs, limited safe zones, on top of Gorilla Grodd's own mechanics.

sections.title: Other mechanics:
items: Gorilla Grodd may do an AOE red cone attack. Avoid this red area or the area in front of him when he does this - in elite it will likely do heavy damage or KO the player. There is a similar attack where Gorilla Grodd will stand on his hands and kick in the air, which does heavy damage as well.

Gorilla Grodd may charge towards a random player on occasion ( Charge Attack). Upon impact this will do large damage and knockback, in the elite version it may KO. It is possible to get out of the way of the charge in time so pay attention.

Adds will spawn in the fight, which should be KO'd ASAP either by the DPS or if someone has been transformed into a gorilla. Be also mindful that Gorilla Grenadiers will spawn around the edges of the room and throw bombs towards the group ( Barrel Toss). They can be troublesome especially when players return from a ship and are unprepared for a bomb to be thrown at them.

After Gorilla Grodd has been defeated the group travel through more streets and battle through add waves of Nightmare Citizens, as well as some familiar Iconic villains such as Trickster, Mirror Master or Killer Frost. Eventually the group reaches a large area outside the Flash Museum where the last two boss encounters are located.

sections.title: Second boss: The Rogues
items: Fairly straightforward fight in both regular and elite - unless the group is trying for the Superior Simultaneous Showdown feat in the elite version then it can become tricky.

It is highly recommended for the tank to use the Super-Speed Movement Mode supercharge Dash Attack, as adds/subbosses can spawn from very far away and head towards the group, and if they are not aggro'd in time they can attack unsuspecting group members.
You may not see all bosses in the same encounter, however below is a list of the bosses you may encounter and their mechanics.
Remember the room is extremely large for an instanced content boss encounter, so mechanics should be avoidable if the player/s are focused.
Adds may be present or spawn along with any sub bosses.
Mechanics:
Heat Wave:
Heat Wave may move to a particular player and punch the ground ( Melee Attack), creating an orange fire AOE on the ground. This does considerable damage over time so it is best to avoid this.
Heat Wave may spawn a red AOE on the ground which again generates a fire AOE.
Fire Ball: Heat Wave may shoot several fire balls around which will explode after they have travelled a certain distance. They are easy to avoid but if a player is hit directly they will take damage.
Captain Cold:

Snowball: Captain Cold will fire several boulders of ice in several directions around him at the same time. Does moderate damage to a player if hit directly, but easy to avoid especially the further away the player is from Captain Cold.
Captain Cold may spawn a large red AOE tell along with a big ice AOE. This deals damage over time to affected players (more info needed)
Pied Piper:
It is best practice to stay max range of Pied Piper where possible and spread out from other players.
Pied Piper may summon an Alley Rat add to assist it in battle. There will be onscreen text when this occurs stating: "Pied Piper Summons a Rat!"

Joyous Musical Balls: Pied Piper will have a red skull icon above his head before playing his flute. While he plays his flute white music orbs will move away from him around the map. Try to avoid these if possible. If a player is hit directly by this they will take moderate damage, and be trapped and stunned, however if other players are nearby to the initial affected player they may take considerable damage. In the elite version this can KO. It is also best practice that if you are stunned by this not to breakout close to other players. (More info needed)
The Top:

Tornado Attack: The Top will spin and spawn green/yellow tornadoes which will move through the map. Avoid these tornadoes. It is also best practice to spread out from other players as you may be given an aura that does damage over time. This will do more damage to you if you are close to another player who also has the same aura.
Captain Boomerang:

Whirling Boomerang: Captain Boomerang may spawn a red ring AOE around him that will then spawn Boomerangs. These deal moderate damage over time to players affected in the regular version and heavy damage over time in the elite version.
Boomerang Cascade: (More info needed)
Gravity Boomerang: (Elite only) Captain Boomerang may spawn a yellow AOE, which will deal damage over time to affected players and crowd control them, drawing them towards the middle of the AOE.

Captain Boomerang may have a red arrow tell on the floor in front of him towards a targeted player. He will then charge towards that player. This will deal considerable damage to the affected player if not evaded in time.
Trickster:
Trickster Tickler: Gas AOE that does damage over time if affected.
Trickster may occasionally teleport to a player and do heavy melee damage.
Mass Hypnosis (1): Trickster may occasionally do this attack to a nearby player. Does moderate damage.
Mirror Master:

Mirror Master will spawn mirrors and mirror images of himself, which will be an annoyance and split damage that the DPS are dealing towards him. You will want to target lock the real Mirror Master (you will know this as the Active Gameplay HUD with his name will be in yellow) and deal single target damage towards him. Be aware he may teleport from time to time. (On PS, Hold L1 to target lock)

Mass Hypnosis (2): Mirror Master will look at a random player while having a red skull icon above his head, before dealing an attack to that player, dealing moderate damage (1-2 ticks of damage) and grounding the affected player. It may also cause the player to be knocked back a little.

sections.title: Last boss: Abra Kadabra, Nightmare Flash and Weather Wizard
items: Fairly straightforward fight in both regular and elite.
Mechanics:
Nightmare Flash:

Whirling Arms: Nightmare Flash may teleport to a random player and do a cone attack, which may pull players in and do large damage. In the elite version this can KO players. This can be stopped by a player lunging Nightmare Flash to interrupt this ability. (On PS, Hold Square to lunge) Try not to give Nightmare Flash immunity when he does this, otherwise in elite it can potentially cause several KOs and possibly a group wipe.

Vibrato: Nightmare Flash has a skull above his head, along with text on-screen telling you that you should block this attack. Anyone in range who doesn't block this attack in time will be KO'd especially in the elite version. (On PS, Hold R1 to block)
It is best practice to not be in melee range of Nightmare Flash.
Weather Wizard:

Weather Wizard has various AOE attacks that do moderate damage, including a large red AOE ( Blizzard), and another AOE ( Tornado Attack). It is best practice to stay max range of Weather Wizard otherwise not many mechanics to speak of.
Abra Kadabra:
Abra Kadabra may teleport to other parts of the map to summon large statue adds to assist him in the fight. This usually occurs after he has taken some damage.
Again like with Weather Wizard if you stay max range of Abra Kadabra when he is near the group then not many mechanics to speak of.

Mana Ball: Sometimes Abra Kadabra may fire white electrical projectiles around. These may do considerable damage and knock back players if they are hit directly - but they are also quite easy to avoid.
Various statue adds may spawn in the fight, as long as they are kept aggro'd by the tank and the rest of the group stay max range of them then they shouldn't be too much of an issue.
Once you have defeated this boss encounter the fight is over and you have completed the raid.
