sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Help out civilians and cops and stop thugs. After a few of them, a dark red tornado briefly appears in the next encounter, coating both civilians, cops and thugs in shiny metal, causing them to all attack you. Defeat a few of them until you are told to go to the Flash Museum, and you must defeat the first boss outside its doors: Metal Mirror Master.

He is not much of a threat himself, dealing fairly low damage, but after he falls under about 70% health, Mysterious Forces (orange vortexes) would open up at your current location every few seconds, dealing heavy continuous damage (12000+ per hit). You only get a moment's notice to dodge and avoid all damage. The vortexes are so frequent it is likely you would have to be on the run constantly.

After defeating him, go inside, where you find The Flash running on the cosmic treadmill. Relieve him and Red Death appears, explaining he is a dark fusion of Batman and Flash from another universe. You are told to use Rogue tech to give you an edge. In order to reach them, you have to fix a shorted door in the southeast corner of the museum.

Before you go there, when you go through the room with the green Investigations, interact with the box on the opposite corner to the Investigation to obtain spare parts you will need, so you don't have to double back to get it once you reach the door.

You have to solve a simple logic puzzle to open the door. There are four portraits, representing wind (Weather Wizard), fire (Heatwave), sound (Pied Piper), and ice (Captain Cold). The order is different every time, and you have to arrange them in a certain order, which is done by interacting with portrait A, and then interacting with portrait B, which switches their positions. A note behind the portraits give you a few hints:
Fire can't be moved.
Sound can't touch fire.
Ice can't touch fire OR ice can't touch sound?

Consider the possible starting position in the image. Since fire (in position 4 from the left) can't be moved and sound can't touch fire, sound must be in position 1 or 2. The two conditions on the third point is impossible to both satisfy. If you switch wind and sound, sound is not touching fire, and ice is not touching fire. If the door still won't unlock, you know the real condition to the third point is actually ice can't touch sound. So, by switching wind and ice, ice is no longer touching sound, and the door unlocks.
You can choose one out of the four Rogue tech. You can go back to this room to switch any time. They will give you different buffs, and can aid you against mobs and finally Red Death.
Ice will create a field that roots mobs and slows down Red Death when he moves through it, preventing his dash attack.
Sound will create a field that stuns mobs and Red Death alike, and allowing you to defuse his bombs.
Wind will reduce damage taken by 75% when triggered, and reflects his Explosive Batarangs.
Fire periodically knocks down nearby enemies and provide a small shield (2000 damage) when hit, and interrupts and knocks down Red Death if he attempts to use his Super Speed Multi-Punch.
Red Death fights like a typical speedster, moving in blinding speed and hitting quite hard. He uses Martial Arts.
Whirling Arm: Unleashing a continuous horizontal tornado that pushes opponents back. Vulnerable to interrupt.
Super Speed Multi-Punch: Blinks around target repeatedly, doing heavy damage.
Explosive Batarang
Dash: Red Death dashes from side to side of the room randomly, encased in a red aura, dealing massive damage and knocking down any opponent hit. Does not seem to use it when slowed by ice.
Bombs: Lays a field of bombs all over the room, can only be defused with sound tech. There is enough room to avoid them, but standing in place risks being hit by Mysterious Forces.
Mysterious Forces will also appear similar to in Mirror Master's fight, but deals about half as much damage.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Talk to Hawkgirl to start a cutscene in which the heroes discuss the situation, culminating in Hawkgirl saying she can't see how this could be any worse. Right on cue, Batman Who Laughs boom tubes in with Dark Robins and dumps a comatose Batman in front of him before leaving. Defeat the Dark Robins while the heroes figure out Batman is rigged to a bomb and you must go into his mind to save him.

You arrive at a mental version of the Batcave. Inside are 5 spots each connected to one of the Dark Knights; 2 random ones are marked by a swarm of black bats, and cause the corresponding Dark Knight to appear. You must defeat the first before the second can appear.
The Batman Who Laughs - giant Joker card, now with Batman Who Laughs' likeness
The Merciless - giant penny, with The Merciless' head on it instead
Dawnbreaker - dinosaur, which is a green construct instead of a real one.
The Drowned - dark water at bottom of Batcave (near the stairs down to the water)

Afterwards, go up to the Batcomputer platform to defend Batman from the Dark Knights. The next location is a theatre where he is attacked by illusions of the Batfamily (2 consoles before the theatre allow you to skip the cutscene, both players must activate one each). If Batman is KO'ed at any point, you are given a short time to rally him, and if he is not rallied, Batman will instantly KO you.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Prime Battleground is a Tier 1 Raid introduced in The Battle for Earth and is the location of the pinnacle of Brainiac's plan to reshape the Multiverse in his own image using the acquired power from his three Prime-Avatars. Infiltrating and boring into the Earth's core from within the grounds of the bottled GCPD Headquarters, both heroes and villains amass together to stop the galactic tyrant's plans before all reality is bent to his will.
The Prime Battleground is directly accessible via a teleporter in the Meta Wing.

sections.title: In-Game History
items: While bottling any possible buildings, Brainiac chose the GCPD Headquarters to bore in to the ground to get to the Nexus of Reality. The Justice League of America recruits New Heroes and New Villiains to search around South Gotham in order to find Brainiac and his hideout.
Finding it out, the JLA orders the New Heroes to go the GCPD Headquarters to end Brainiac in the one now known as "The Prime Battleground"

After Brainiac's defeat, Future Lex Luthor takes advantage of the portal that Brainiac dug upon reaching the center of the Multiverse, The Nexus of Reality. Future Batman follows Lex and, later, Future Batman and Future Lex will recruit New Heroes and New Villains respectively to assist in foiling the other.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: You must defeat the Prime Avatars of Tech, Meta and Magic. Only one is targetable at one time - the other two would always be in stasis beams and cannot be attacked.

It is highly recommended to have your raid composed of a diversity of power types due to conflicts that occur between the same powers such as the poison from two Nature players, the burn effect from two fire characters and the Circle of Protection/Destruction from two Sorcery Healers/DPSs.
Damage Role
Keep damaging each adds and/or avatars and watch out for spike hits from avatars.; It is recommended to stay at range as the Avatars' strong hits are at melee to mid-range.
IF the group agrees, assist in taking out the spawners.; Try not to shutdown the Magic spawner before the Brainiac fight, if so, even before the Brainiac fight, Healer drones will appear.
Healer Role
STAY ON YOUR TOES!. There is no telling when one of your teammates will receive spike damage.
Tank Role
Tank each Avatar as you would in their original raids.
Controller Role
Give out as much power to the group, as they need it.
Debuff bosses, especially defense, attack, and health. For Brainiac, debuff heal,and attack.
Avatar of Tech

"Power Blast"(Single target) - He will target a single player, and release a strong hit from 1.5k-3k. It cannot be dodged and it is marked as a red circle under your foot, to decrease damage, use shields or just block.
"Radius Bomb"(AOE) - An orange crosshair/ reticule will appear in an area, this is dodgeable, as it stays in one spot. If not dodged, it can wipe out a number of players in one time.
"Rocket Shower/Gun Storm" - He will spin around shooting many rockets up to the air dealing multiple 800- 1000s to around it.
Avatar of Meta

"Purple Ball" - Every so often he will fire purple balls at players, they will inflict massive damage so be sure Roll away or block if you don't have enough time to.(He will fire 1-2 balls every time he uses this attack.)

"Electricity" - With this attack Meta releases pockets of electricity on the floor of the battlefield it is necessary that players immediately roll away as it will usually spawn directly under some players.

"Summon Tentacle" - Similar to the tail like lightning that appears around the Prime Battleground, one of these will appear behind Meta as impales is whips into the ground, the entire raid is advised to simple back as far away from him until this attack subsides.
Avatar of Magic

"Flame of Change: Claws of the Lion" - He will be powered by lion skills and capabilities showing claws and the head of a lion.; Special moves:; Pounce - He will pounce as said to a player and continously bite them.

"FoC: Wings of the Eagle" - He will be powered by eagle skills and maneuverability showing wings.; Special moves:; Whirlwind - Spin around in circles pulling players and damaging over time.(Roll immediately.); High Pressure - Pull players closing to it, opening a chance for a finish.
"Flame of Change: Fusion" - Powered by both lion and eagle, having all their skills.
The Final Battle :Brainiac
A straightforward battle, just keep damaging and debuffing him.
Brainiac has all three Avatars' powers, so combine all the tactics above to complete use.
At every quarter of his health(75%, 50%, 25%) He will strike a pulse, knocking back and summoning healer drones that will heal him continously, just take them out.
Controller Role: Attack and healing Debuffs
Healers: Stay far, as the group depends on you, if you die , the group will have to restart.
DPS: Burn him as fast as you can.
Tank: Tank the remaining mobs if there is still, if not, focus on Brainiac.

sections.title: Overview
items: Rage Impurity is a Tier 3 4-player villain Operation in the War of the Light Part II DLC.

sections.title: Act 1
items: The operation begins with you and your team arriving on Ranx, who has been overrun with Red Lanterns. You and your team must clear them all out. Once you do, you will find Sinestro is the west room. He is held down by Furious Ursa, who is the first subboss of the operation. To bring it down, you must neutralize the Crimson Mists in the Central Power Battery. Bleez will be in the battery to try and stop you, by the way. And finally, Defeat Atrocitus after his shield is brung down. After he is defeated, Sinestro thanks you for purifying and defending the Qward Power Battery and the operation ends.

" Ares never wanted anything to do with the Underworld, he used Hades as a pawn to get to my mother. With no king, the Shades are unruly and the Underworld in shambles. We need to find Hades and restore him to his rightful place as ruler." — Wonder Woman
" Without a ruler, the Underworld is a mess. Hades is the only one who can bring order back to this dank place... And I'll need him at full power in order to help take down Typhon." — Circe
Raising Hades is a duo accessible from the On Duty menu and part of the Amazon Fury Part III episode.

sections.title: Story
items: Travel to the Greek Underworld and restore Hades as the Lord of the Dead.

There is trouble in the Underworld. And there’s a good deal of trouble beginning to brew on Olympus. It’s become clear that Hades needs to be back on his throne as the rightful Lord of the Dead, but to get him there, you’re going to need to intervene. Head to the Underworld and try to stop the chaos, but be alert! Who knows what sort of monsters are waiting as you attempt restore Hades as Lord of the Dead and seek his aid in regaining Olympus.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Once you arrive, go down the stairs, defeating the beasts along the way, and you'll find yourself in the arena of the first subboss.

sections.title: First Subboss: Nest of Harpies
items: You must defeat the two harpies to proceed. Look around and notice two harpy nests: one of the ground near the passage to the next area, and another on the higher level between two braziers. They'll be important during the fight.
Aello the Swift uses Dual Wield and One-Handed weapons and owns the upper nest, while Celaeno the Dark uses a Shield and owns the lower nest. Beyond that, they use the following abilities:
Healing Contrivance: a type of "health stealer" ability that heals the caster over time while damaging the target.
Wing Buffet : fly around a marked target, lifting them up and causing damage over time.
Ground Slam: Aello spins while in the air, pressuring the ground to damage nearby enemies.
Leeching Field: Celaeno places a circle of purple flames around her target that burns and deals damage over time.

From time to time, the harpies will stop fighting and encase themselves in purple shields, and a message will appear "Harpies are Summoning Dark Magic!" Each of the nests will spawn a purple Dark Crystal (remember who owns each nest), from which the harpies will absorb power after a few seconds. Destroy the crystals to interrupt their summoning and continue the fight. They can be defeated in any order and won't revive each other.
After defeating the harpies, descend further until you find the Hellhounds.

sections.title: Second Subboss: Trio of Hell Hounds
items: Now, you must get rid of these hounds. Note that the bigger one, Orthrus, has an aura around his head, which signals his special ability: a howl that revives his allies, Barghest and Old Shuck, with around 40% of their health. Besides that, the Hellhounds abilities are:
Dog Bite Toss
Fling: Chomps down on the target and toss them to the side.
Leeching Field: Flames appear around Barghest and Old Shuck once they're down. It'll burn the player and deal damage over time.
Pounce
Ranged Attack
Ravage
Savage Bite: The hound will violently bite a marked target. Lethal when coming from Orthrus.
Terrifying Bark
Thrash: Snaps at the target, damaging it over time and stunning it.

After banishing the Hellhounds, go down the path defeating the shades along the way, and you'll find a weakened Hades ahead. Interact with him to set him free, and listen to his speech until the end. Then, follow him to the final boss.

sections.title: Final Boss: Ixion
items: You'll find Ixion burning with a green flame and two of his allies encased in green shields. Look around and notice that the four braziers in the area have the same shields. Engage the shades that are vulnerable and the shields around the flames will become targetable. You must break the shields and interact with the braziers to extinguish the fire to get to Ixion - the use of shields is recommended, as more shades will come as you defeat them.

Ixion uses a Two-Handed weapon, and summons shades to fight alongside him. He has one special ability, Ground Slam: he'll smash the ground with his hammer, causing a localized earthquake that'll deal heavy damage - this ability is not announced. Avoid the earthquake and defeat the shades if they come between you and Ixion - they'll arrive in groups of three, but Hades will help you by banishing one of from each wave. Once you defeat the False Lord, the remaining shades will vanish, and Hades will banish Ixion.
Speak to Hades to finish the run.

title: Riot Control Prototype
summary: The Riot Control Prototype ( R.C.P.) is a large spider drone designed to fend off invaders within the Batcave: Outer Caverns.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Riot Control Prototype ( R.C.P.) is a large spider drone designed to fend off invaders within the Batcave: Outer Caverns.
The drone is the first boss encountered in the Batcave: Outer Caverns raid.

sections.title: Involvement
items: Brother Eye and Brainiac have taken over the Batcave's mainframe and, along with it, the substantial automated defense and security forces. Both heroes and villains battle against Earth's real enemy in this 8-player raid.

sections.title: Combat Tips
items: Additional spider drones constantly enter the arena to aid it - one tank and damage dealer should be committed to killing these or they will overwhelm the raid. These drones will attempt to incapacitate their targets with foam - players must move until the foam on their body disappears or they will be stunned and take heavy damage.

sections.title: Phase One
items: The R.C.P. will begin by releasing mines and firing its machineguns. When enough health is lost, it will enter the next phase.

sections.title: Phase Two
items: At 50% hp, the fight will enter phase two. In this phase there will be a new add type, Ambush Drones, which will perma-stun their target until interrupted. These need to be focused as incapacitating a tank or healer can easily wipe the raid.

sections.title: Phase Three
items: After being brough down to about 10% health, the R.C.P. will activate a shield, making it invulnerable. To finish it off the raid must first destroy the newly spawned Flashbang Drones and throw the grenades they drop at the boss. Players should look for clear shots, as the flashbangs will detonate on the first hit and too many misses will cause the boss to enrage and wipe the raid.

RN: Book of the Black is a Tier 7 Raid in the Raging Night chapter. It also features a Casual, Elite, and Elite Plus versions. The alert RN: Book of the Black Alert is a scaled-down version of this instance.
Story-wise, this instance coincides with the alert version, and precedes events in the challenge RN: Nekron's Lair.
Voivode returns to help you in your quest against the Black Lanterns! Follow her to discover the whereabouts of Sinestro to shore up your ranks against the great threat.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: You must rescue Sinestro and Larfleeze from the Book the Black so the light of all corps can be combined to create a White Lantern to combat the Black Lantern threat. In the alert version, the Sinestro segment is skipped and he can be freed immediately.

sections.title: Sinestro
items: There are 8 pillars around the area each projecting a red beam into the sky. Defeat Scribes, each carrying a rune, and interact with them after they are defeated to take their rune. Then interact with the pillar of the same rune to deactivate it until all are shut down. Each pillar requires 2 runes - you need to use the currently glowing red rune on them. Therefore, you need a total of 16 runes. The right runes may not be immediately available and you'd have to keep defeating Scribes until you get the right one.

There are two Zombie Abomination fights, one before and one after freeing Sinestro. However, the second one can be easily lured onto the bridge and then off into the water - the water does not harm players if they fall in (although it would instant KO pets), but will instantly KO the Zombie Abomination.

sections.title: Larfleeze
items: Larfleeze's hoard has been robbed by his own orange lanterns. Defeat the orange lanterns and Treasure Hoarders hiding in the area, take the hoard and carry them back to Larfleeze until his hoard is fully restored.
Attempt to retrieve the orange lantern battery, and Avaricious Glomulus appears. Defeat him to complete this section.

sections.title: Lyssa Drak
items: Lyssa Drak starts with a shield that makes her immune to damage. The mechanic is similar to the Sinestro pillar segment. The Book of the Black displays a line of runes, all black instead of the current one, which is in red. Defeat Scribes to obtain the runes matching the red rune and interact with the Book to proceed. Once the whole line is fulfilled, Lyssa can be damaged. After a while, her immunity would return and you would need to do it again.
Lyssa Drak fights with One-Handed and has an orbital strike-like attack consisting of multiple yellow beams.

Runes on defeated Scribes have an expire timer. When picked up, you cannot see a timer, but it will still eventually expire. However, the timer is refreshed on pick up. Since there is no harm in carrying a rune - you can override with a new rune if necessary - you can pick up a rune which is about to expire and hold it, if it is going to be useful next.
There is a bug where the Scribe with the required rune does not spawn for many waves - possibly triggered by a rune expiring on a player. A team wipe is required to reset it.
Once defeated, Lyssa Drak flees. However, in the walk-in solo version, Black Lantern Voivode shows up to kill her, and denies her a Black Lantern ring.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: After Sinestro and Larfleeze are rescued in RN: Book of the Black, you must enter Nekron's Lair to find Atrocitus and defeat Nekron.

sections.title: Voivode
items: Note: This section, along with segments where you aid Carol and Indigo-1, were originally part of the challenge but seems to have been removed, possibly due to the length being too long for a challenge.

You find Saint Walker battling Voivode, who is holding Atrocitus prisoner. Voivode fights with Dual Wield. A particularly annoying mechanic is her black energy chains which hard stuns (requires button mashing) which can prevent you from avoiding Zombie Bursters that suicide bomb you for massive damage.

This fight can be beaten by simply staying away and allowing your NPC allies to do all the work (this is easier to do by letting Voivode KO you first to ensure Kyle and Carol are attacking her). She does not summon mobs if fought this way. As long as you hit Voivode at the end before she is defeated, you gain loot as usual. This works even in elite.
Upon defeating Voivode, she regenerates but Saint Walker and Carol Ferris keeps her contained. Atrocitus flies off to confront Nekron alone.

sections.title: Barriers
items: After defeating Voivode, you meet Sinestro and Larfleeze there is a scripted defeat section - you are told to defend Larfleeze while he maintains a barrier against the zombies to the south, but eventually lots of zombies appear north of the barrier - on your side - and you are told to flee to the north. However, progress in the challenge is achieved by defeating the mobs attacking Larfleeze. The mobs attacking the barrier do not actually reduce the barrier meter. Even if you defeat all the mobs to the south, you are still told to flee. Therefore, do not engage them.

There, you meet Saint Walker and Carol again, with a similar barrier mechanic - the barriers' meters are reduced not by mob attacks from outside on the wall, but by you, Indigo-1, and Kyle Rayner defeating mobs on your side. Even if Saint Walker or Carol are KO'd, it does not affect the barrier meter. So again, only fight the mobs inside the barrier until the barrier meter is down, and fall back further north as instructed.

Finally, Kyle Rayner will conjure a barrier of his own, although it works slightly differently in that the meter will drop and the wall will come down even if you do not fight, at which point a cutscene starts. Atrocitus appears - and he fires a beam at you, joined by all other corps members, turning you into a White Lantern.

sections.title: Nekron
items: As a White Lantern, you have unique combos (similar to Brawling melee and Hand Blast ranged) and abilities.

Scintillating Blast: Fires 3 orbs in a narrow cone that explodes on targets hit, dealing damage in a small area, and can one-shot basic Zombies and Zombie Bursters. It is not recommended to use weapon attacks because this ability has no cooldown and deals way more damage, and should be spammed constantly as you move forward to mow down the zombies.

Luminous Beam: Fires a targeted beam at a single enemy, knocking them back and dealing damage (the knockback can cause them to fall out of range of the damage). This can be used to one-shot Zombie Bloaters and Black Lantern Reavers that take greatly reduced damage from Scintillating Blast.
Radiant Nova: Deals damage in an area and knocks back. Scintillating Blast is generally already sufficient, but Radiant Nova can be useful against Reavers while Luminous Beam is on cooldown.
Brilliant Chains: Stuns the target and chains to nearby enemies, all are stunned and dealt damage over time. As this is slow, it is not recommended for basic mobs.
Life Shield: Shield Power that also heals you a moderate amount.

You do not actually have to defeat the huge groups of undead - you can simply fly straight to the boss (supersonic is not available however). Most mobs will ignore you if you are high in the air. Luminous Beam can be used to deal with flying Reavers, and Life Shield prevents them from slowing you down (while other Shield Powers can't be used, Ally: John Constantine's shield on trinket activation may still be useful).

You face Nekron and Black Lantern Voivode. It is recommended to defeat Voivode first, because she does not respawn throughout the fight and can be taken out quickly, reducing a lot of pressure from incoming damage. Defeat Nekron for the first time, and you're instructed to hit the black lantern battery. There is only a limited time window to do so before Nekron fully heals himself, and you have to do this again - and Nekron will start summoning mobs and have additional attacks.

Dark Bolt: You are prompted to block, which greatly reduces the damage from this attack. During the prompt, you can stun Nekron (e.g. with Brilliant Chains) to cancel his attack. An active Life Shield would act as if you are blocking for this purpose.
Dark Blast: Black Lantern symbol appears on floor, after a few seconds it erupts dealing potentially one-shot damage.

Nekron only flies in the first stage prior to you defeating him the first time. Mobs are usually focused on your allies but they can generally be taken out fairly easily with Luminous Beam (for straggler Reavers) and Radiant Nova (for zombies and general purpose good area damage). You can also hide on top of the black lantern battery if you need time to recover. Radiant Nova's cooldown is slightly shorter than the time window where you can damage the battery and it hits very hard - so if you time it to use Radiant Nova immediately after it becomes vulnerable, you can squeeze in 2 casts and do substantially more damage.

It shouldn't take more than 4-5 Nekron defeats to destroy the battery (try to fight him near the battery so you don't waste precious time going over to it), and the battle is won. Afterwards, Sinestro suggests that you have the power to resurrect Voivode, and you do, and she is overjoyed. Kyle indicates she was acting as Nekron's Black Hand anchoring him, so with her resurrected, Nekron is banished.

sections.title: Trivia
items: During this challenge, a "You have slain Klaatu!" popup may appear, a reference to Klaatu from the film The Day the Earth Stood Still. The Day the Island Stood Still also refers to this.

Prior to becoming a White Lantern, the Black Lantern Reavers tend to ignore the player, and focus on flying back and forth. They would try to return to this routine even when in combat with the player.

references.label: The Day the Island Stood Still

title: S.T.A.R. Labs Research Facility (Alert)
summary: S.T.A.R. Labs Research Facility is a Tier 1 Alert in the Fight for the Light Episode accessible after reaching Level 30.

sections.title: Overview
items: S.T.A.R. Labs Research Facility is a Tier 1 Alert in the Fight for the Light Episode accessible after reaching Level 30.

Brainiac is attempting to claim the power of the emotional spectrum at the S.T.A.R. Labs Research Facility, having constructed a Brainiac-styled giant Yellow Power Battery there. Throughout the facility, you can hear Parallax whispering to you...

sections.title: Background
items: Brainiac has hacked a S.T.A.R. Labs Research Facility to tap into the powers of the Green and Yellow Lanterns. Players must stop Brainiac from unlocking the secrets of the Emotional Spectrum and prevent Parallax from possessing Arkillo, Kilowog, Sinestro, and Hal Jordan to escape its prison in the Yellow Battery.

sections.title: Story
items: Brainiac has invaded S.T.A.R. Labs and is co-opting their research on the emotional spectrum. The Green Lantern and Sinestro Corps need all the help they can get to stop him.

sections.title: Walkthough
items: Green Lanterns and Sinestro Corps have agreed to a truce in order to face the Brainiac threat together. You must find Sinestro in the facility - you need to active 7 reactors, clearing out mobs on the way. One you find him, you need to defeat three Manhunters that now serve Brainiac.

Then, in the largest western chamber that looks like it is overgrown with colossal fungi, battle the Scion of Will/Scion of Fear, a Brainiac construct, on top of the platforms (there are jump pads to help non-fliers reach them).
Upon defeat, it explodes into 3 components, which must each be transported to stations A, then, B, then C.

Finally, you return the the central chamber - where it turns out the Brainiac battery is holding Parallax, the entity of Fear. It then possesses Kilowog, Arkillo, Sinestro, and Hal Jordan one by one in turn, and you must defeat them all. When they are all defeated, Parallax retreats and the Brainiac Lantern explodes.

title: Starro: Spindrift Station
summary: Starro: Spindrift Station is a Tier 5, 8-player Raid in the Deluge episode. It requires a Combat Rating of 210+ for the Normal and Elite versions, while the Casual version requires Level 15+.

sections.title: Overview
items: Sunstone Fragment
Starro: Spindrift Station is a Tier 5, 8-player Raid in the Deluge episode. It requires a Combat Rating of 210+ for the Normal and Elite versions, while the Casual version requires Level 15+.
It was also available as a Tier 7 Flashback Raid SoA Flashback: Spindrift Station in Shadows Over Argo during chapter events. It featured a Casual, Normal, and Elite version.
Warning: This article might contain spoilers!

sections.title: Story
items: Head to the Spindrift Station Gala Event.

sections.title: Background
items: The Spindrift Station is an Atlantean Dry Land Embassy built on the shoreline of Massachusetts. As an Atlantean embassy the station is a personal project of Aquaman's who intended to improve relations between the sea kingdom and the surface.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: When you first get into the raid, you must first speak to Mera. She will tell you to enjoy the gala and then talk to her when you're ready. She will be on the balcony on the west side of the hall. After a conversation between her and Aquaman about the Starro attacks, a bomb explodes next to the balcony and Manta suddenly appears and swears revenge on Aquaman. You must defeat him.

sections.title: Black Manta
items: Periodically during the battle, he plants a dozen or so Black Manta Mines. They are always placed in a large circle in the middle of the area, regardless of where he is. You will be instructed to break a chain reaction that will be caused by them by interacting with at least one of them quickly. If you fail, the whole team will be KO'd instantly, regardless if you're a tank or if you have a shield on you. If you defuse at least some of them, you will take much less damage.
After you defeat Black Manta, Corum Rath suddenly appears and states that the people of Atlantis demand change, and he is that change. He plans to destroy Spindrift Station, and you must stop him.

sections.title: Pipe puzzle
items: You must get through waves of enemies, and then come across a flooded room. Two of the players must drain the flooded room from both sides to continue.

First, players must insert one oxygen tank in both sides before two players can go in. Each of them must solve a simple pipe puzzle - you will be given a number of pipe pieces, one by one, and you must carry it to the wall where the pipe is. Each piece you are given can only go to a fixed spot you will be directed to.

Then, you must rotate the pre-existing pieces so they all connect into a single continuous pipe. Once complete, you need to interact with the the big wheel in the middle of the wall to finish up. During that time, your oxygen supply will drain. If it reaches zero, the entire team will be KO'd (it is possible for oxygen to hit zero right as the wheel finishes turning, which KO'es you but the puzzle is considered finished).

Brine creatures will also appear in the flooded rooms and try to slow your progress, and being hit will cause additional oxygen drain. During this time, all abilities including pets and trinkets are disabled and replaced by a single ability that disables brine creatures at the cost of 10 oxygen. Braine creatures' attacks also deal regular damage and it is nearly impossible to restore health, with healers outside not being able to heal you either.
Outside the flooded rooms, players must add more oxygen supply when needed. Mobs will also attack the oxygen supply which must be defended.

sections.title: Morgwar
items: After you drain the room, you must take on more waves of enemies, and then you will be at the end of the raid. Corum Rath summons the rogue water elemental, Morgwar. He then escapes and leaves Morgwar to deal with the players. You must defeat Morgwar to finish the raid.
Periodically, Morgwar would flatten into a pool of water, immune to all damage. However, it will keep dragging players nearby towards it, damaging them.

After you defeat Morgwar, Mera instructs you to leave Spindrift Station, as it is collapsing. She also states that she will go find Aquaman and right after that, Aquaman appears. He also tells you to leave, and the raid ends.

sections.title: Flashback
items: Relieve a past memory from under the sea.Head to the Spindrift Station Gala Event.

This raid was featured as a Flashback instance only during the release of Children of Krypton, Chapter 1: Shadows Over Argo, listed under the name SoA Flashback: Spindrift Station. The original version remained available for all players.

The difficulty of the instance was increased to match the other Tier 7 instances in the chapter, rewarding chapter-related items and currency. The Collectibles obtainable in the original raid can also be found in this one.

Spindrift Station was chosen as a Flashback raid for Shadows Over Argo due to the presence of Aquaman, Mera, Ocean Master, and Black Manta in both contents, and it is located underwater like Sunken Argo City.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The disastrous launch of the Spindrift Station is one of the reasons why Aquaman was later deposed by Corum Rath in Atlantis: Royal Palace.
While sections of the station are sealed and completely filled with water to serve the more aquatic Atlanteans, the station also reserved "Dry Rooms" for meetings with surface visitors.
While all instances in Deluge have the prefix "Starro", this raid is the only that does not directly involve Starros in any capacity.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Hal Jordan states that Ion - the entity of willpower - must be restored. Sinetro urges him to get a move on as they have learned carrying the Spark of an entity rapidly drains the energy from power rings.

As you battle through the Orange Lanterns, Hal assures other Green Lanterns that Sinestro is helping them, and comments that he knows deep down Sinestro misses working together with him, but the latter replies that he is still the superior, to Hal's disdain.
After clearing them out, you can enter the chamber and fight Avaricious Captain Cold. There is a restoration barrel in the northeast corner. Then, operate the machinery to reach a different level.
Sinestro forms a barrier to stop further Orange Lantern incursions while you must defeat the rest in the chamber so Hal can recharge his ring. Defeat Avaricious Cheetah.

Afterwards, Hal says that he must give the spark to you temporarily. Take it, then defeat more Orange Lanterns until Ion can be restored. However, Glomulus ambushes you, and Hal says he can't recharge due to Ion's weakened state. Defeat him. Hal expresses his gratitude, and says Sinestro thanks you too, which the latter stonily denies.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The story of this instance is followed by Zamaron Conversion Chamber.
At the start of the instance, Glomulus can be seen through the north window in the next hall, sneaking in.

Due to the outer area being C-shaped, if you draw the Orange Lanterns to one end then use Movement Increasing Skills to rush to the other, they would be stuck in the first end trying to reach you through the wall.

It takes a long time, but it is possible for the Orange Lanterns to KO Hal Jordan and Sinestro. Even when KO'ed, they can be heard saying their voice lines. When you clear out the first Orange Lanterns, you can open the door to the area with Avaricious Captain Cold, and both would be "revived" and fighting, despite still having the revive interact option. They do not take damage during this fight.; In the second level, Sinestro, who is maintaining a shield, can be KO'ed without affecting the shield. When the mobs are defeated, even a KO'ed Hal Jordan would revive himself and recharge, at which point he loses the revive option. Sinestro would automatically be revived as well in the boss fight against Avaricious Cheetah, but this time he can take damage and if KO'ed again, he will do the standard "flee" animation and disappear completely. As his dialogue is required for the story to progress to the point Hal gives you the Spark of Ion, this would make you permanently stuck and unable to finish the instance.; It is also possible for a KO'ed Hal would disappear before recharging, also making you stuck.

title: Starro: Invasion!
summary: Starro: Invasion! is a 4-player alert in the Deluge episode.

sections.title: Overview
items: Starro: Invasion! is a 4-player alert in the Deluge episode.
Access to the instance requires a combat rating of 210 for Normal difficulty or Level 15+ for Casual. The alert rewards 5 Source Marks.
The alert actually takes places in different locations one of which is chosen randomly.

sections.title: Story
items: Starro has taken control of heroes and villains alike, and is forcing them to do his bidding. Put a stop to Starro by rescuing those under its influence.
JSA Headquarters

The Justice Society of America is not responding to distress calls[1]. When the exobyte heroes/villains arrive in the JSA Headquarters, the place was taken by Starro, and members of the JSA are under their control. They fight the alien starfish and teleport Alan Scott, Black Canary, Hawkman, Power Girl, and Wildcat to a S.T.A.R./ LexCorp Lab to have the spores removed from their faces.
STAR Labs Research Facility

The STAR Labs Facility in Little Bohemia has been taken by Starro. The exobyte heroes/villains make their way through the mind-controlled STAR troops and Starros, until they get the attention of a STAR-associated iconic who is under Starro's control. While trying not to lose their mind to Starro themselves, they fight and subdue Cyborg, Martian Manhunter, Professor Zoom, Superman, and Supergirl, teleporting them to a S.T.A.R./ LexCorp Lab to have the spores removed from their faces.
Xanadu's Magic Shop

The exobyte heroes/villains arrive at Madame Xanadu's shop, which is populated by Starro-controlled Sentinels of Magic and cultists from the Cult of Trigon, almost as if Starro has interrupted some sort of conflict between the two factions. The group ventures through the shop defeating the controlled mobs as well as Starros, all the way down to the basement. There they face powerful magic users: Brother Blood, Donna Troy, Felix Faust, Solomon Grundy, and Zatanna. Victorious, they send them to a S.T.A.R./ LexCorp Lab to have the spores removed from their faces.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: In every location, you should defeat all of the enemies to get access to open the door to the next area, then clean the final room so the controlled iconic will appear. Have in mind that the mobs in this instance hit harder than the ones in most alerts - it is recommended to use a strong shield or have at least a tank or healer on your group.

The Starro mob is found in all scenarios. They come in the varieties Ordinary, Powerful, Mender, and Spitter. Ordinary Starros are the smallest and weakest of them, they use only Hand Blast attacks, while the others are larger and use Starro Beam. Powerful Starros deal more damage, Starro Menders are healers able to heal themselves and nearby allies. It is possible to not get all of them in a run. Starro Spitters are controllers that will attempt to knock down and stun.

For the controlled iconics, they have most of the movements you'd be familiar with from previous instances and bounties, plus Starro Beam. Upon defeating the iconic, interact with them to end the run. A chest will appear near where the boss spawned with additional rewards from the original Starro the Conqueror event, and one of the players must interact with them so the group can collect the treasure box.
Be aware that every scenario has its own specificities.

sections.title: JSA Headquarters Scenario
items: JSA Security is the special mob for this scenario. There are 4 types, but you only have to be aware of the Enhanced Security Mechs, as they are much more powerful than the others, with powerful abilities such as Flame Field, Flame Cascade, and Flame Burst - hold block or back away when he starts spinning to avoid massive damage. Once you clean the enemies in the first area, you'll to the next room. While you clean the rest of the mobs, pay attention to the Starros feeding on the energy from the mainframes in the room - they're Starro Sappers and will play a part in boss fight.
Fighting the JSA

Some time after you've engaged the boss, a couple of Starro Sappers will start a countdown. If you don't destroy them, they'll grow up into full Starros and attack you - the bigger the mainframe, the more powerful the Starro (from Callow, to Ordinary, to Powerful) - and they will accumulate if ignored. This mechanic is similar to the one from the fight with in the CCPD station in Stemming the Tide.

Controlled Alan Scott is a little tricky. At first, you would think just using a regular Two-Handed weapon, but the combat log will tell you his damage is caused by "Light Construct: Hammer," which implies it is closest to the Construct Combos from the Light powerset than to mere weapon. He hits hard, and a melee tactic will be risky if you don't have enough health and/or defense, or a shield strong enough to resist his blows.

sections.title: Madame Xanadu's Magic Shop Scenario
items: Controlled Sentinels of Magic (yellow) and Controlled Blood Cultist (red) are the special mob for this scenario. They come in a few varieties, but Warder, Blood Arcanum, Blood Priest Mender, and Blood Cultist Deadeye are the strongest. Most of them attack with wands, while Menders use Hand Blast and Deadeyes use bows. Most of the attacks are vulnerable to interrupt or to block - use movements and abilities that interrupt (such as lunge) or imobilize them if you have enough dominance. Menders can heal themselves.

Once you have cleaned the final room, one of the following magic user bosses will appear: Controlled Brother Blood, Controlled Donna Troy, Controlled Felix Faust, Controlled Solomon Grundy, or Controlled Zatanna.
Magic Shop Bosses

During the boss fight, the magical energy will attract special Starros. Defeating a Powerful Starro Splitter will turn it into 2 Ordinary Starro Splitter; defeating a Ordinary Starro Splitter will turn it into 2 Callow Starros. They'll go to where the battle is, and will accumulate if ignored. Tanks or controllers can help with dealing with the crowd.
Controlled Brother Blood fights with Hand Blast attacks. As you're fighting a weapon user, understanding the dynamics of combat is important to successfully counter and to avoid being countered.

Controlled Zatanna is a strong opponent. She uses flight and a wand that throws Hand Blast attacks when in range and One-Handed attacks in melee. She especializes in ranged attacks that cause high damage. It is recommended to use shields and block.

references.label: vulnerable to interrupt or to block

sections.title: STAR Labs Research Facility Scenario
items: Controlled STAR Labs troops are the special mob for this scenario. There are 2 types: Officer and Lieutenant. The Officer is weaker and uses simple rifle attacks, while the Lieutenant has more health and uses only the "Rifle Shot" attack, a beam that deals significant damage, but is vulnerable to interrupt - use movements and abilities that interrupt (such as lunge) or imobilize them if you have enough dominance.

Once you have cleaned the final room, the floor will be covered with Starro Spores (tiny versions of Starro that can't be attacked) and one of the following STAR Labs related bosses will appear: Controlled Superman, Controlled Cyborg, Controlled Supergirl, Controlled Professor Zoom, or Controlled Martian Manhunter.
Starro Spores

During the boss fight, avoid getting in contact with the spores, as those will make your character mind-controlled - your teammates can reverse that by using a Quicklime Canister near you (this mechanic appears again in the raid Starro: The Threat Below. There are four consoles in the room which can be used and which will clean an area around them of those Starro (below the boss's platform, by the healing barrel to the West, then across the room from this one, and another up under the northernmost of the platforms), but the platform where the iconic boss spawns on cannot be cleaned (if you can fly, you don't have to worry about them unless you're pulled down by the boss or your mind-controlled teammate). When you activate a console, you'll hear the message "Cryogenic fire suppression system initiated. Sub-zero gas activated." If get in the way of the gas, it will stun you, and you'll have to use breakout to escape. Each console can only be used once per fight.
STAR Lab Bosses

Controlled Professor Zoom uses Super Speed and Martial Arts, including attacks that will pull and knock back, throwing you across the room. He makes it harder to avoid the Spores. Use lunge and block to keep him in check (tanks might use their Group Breakout abilities).

Controlled Superman uses Flight and Brawling. He retains Cold Breath and Freezing Breath, but he doesn't use Heat Vision (probably due to the starfish on his face). Fighting him in the air is the easiest option if you have quick reflexes to avoid falling on one of the spores below.

I need you to push out my mother's guards and establish a supply line so that we can keep our allies armed and healthy. When you find a store of supplies, light a beacon, and a squad will be dispatched to collect them and bring them to the docks." — Wonder Woman
Supply Lines is a Tier 2 Duo included in the Amazon Fury Part I Episode.

The Amazons have constructed an Armada of invisible battleships to launch their assault on Gotham City and destroy Brainiac. These ships are being loaded with troops and supplies at the docks of Paradise Island. As a rebel supporter you will need to help Wonder Woman’s forces obtain supplies and ships, while at the same time try to prevent the launch of the enemy's vessels. As a loyalist working with Circe and Hippolyta, you will find yourself defending the war supplies from the rebels and trying to prevent their ships from pursuing your armada to the mortal world.

Supplying the fight in Gotham City is no easy task, and it's where both sides are most vulnerable. Players will need to assist, defending supplies en route and taking on enemies attempting to stop them in the Warehouse Division.
Go to Themyscira to fight for control of the Warehouses and establish vital supply lines of weapons and resources.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Mechanics

Circe's (heroes) / Wonder Woman's (villains) companion in the last fight is decided by the players when choosing a shield and a weapon to equip the Amazon Sentry Statue in order to get access to the palace. This is how it goes:

There are 5 possible minor bosses in the instance: Apollonia the Enchantress(H) / High Priestess Athanasia(V), Megaira of the Pack(H) / Desma of the Pride(V), the Phoenix, the Satyr Trio, and the cyclops Ten-Ton Takis(H) / Infamous Soldier Statue(V). The game will randomly pick one of them to serve as the subboss at the Temple, and another one to guard the statues with the weapons at the Cliffside Gazebo. You'll be left with the remaining 3 to narrow down to 1 for the final boss fight.
Each one of the fighters mentioned above corresponds to a weapon AND a shield. The choice you make will eliminate the correspondent fighter(s).
By picking the shield with:
Cyclops will remove Ten-Ton Takis / Infamous Soldier Statue
Lion will remove Megaira of the Pack / Desma of the Pride
Lady will remove Apollonia the Enchantress / High Priestess Athanasia
Trio of beasts will remove Satyr Trio
Wings will remove Phoenix
By picking the weapon:
Club will remove Ten-Ton Takis / Infamous Soldier Statue
Spear will remove Megaira of the Pack / Desma of the Pride
Mace will remove Apollonia the Enchantress / High Priestess Athanasia
Sword will remove Satyr Trio
Axe will remove Phoenix
Strategy

In practice, you can predict how your run will go as soon as you get to the first subboss' area in order to complete the feat in the most efficient way possible. Identify who the three statues are representing; if none of them are the one you need for the feat, you might want to leave your current run and start a new one. If one or more of them are what you're looking for, be sure to choose the statue that represents the one you DON'T want to see next to Circe/Wonder Woman. Think of this process as crossing items in a list: every time you pick a weapon and a shield, you're crossing them off the final fight.
Example

You are in the hero version of the alert and are sent to find the missing pieces of the Amazon Sentry Statue. You choose the Cliffside path first. The first subboss is Megaira. Behind her, there are 3 statues with their shields with the emblems Wings, Cyclops, and Lady— by process of elimination, that means the Satyr Trio will be the subboss waiting at the Temple. You can choose between the Phoenix, Ten-Ton Takis, and Apollonia for the final fight.
You defeat Megaira and pick Wings, which will remove Phoenix from the final fight.

Then, you to to the Temple and defeat the Satyr Trio. One of the statues holds a Club, while the other holds Mace. You can choose between Ten-Ton Takis and Apollonia. You choose the Mace, thus removing Apollonia from the final fight.
This means Ten-Ton Takis will appear during the final boss fight.

sections.title: Trivia
items: A menagerie is a collection of captive, usually exotic, animals kept for display. It was the precursor of the modern zoo.

The name of this feat is a possible reference to the 1944 play The Glass Menagerie written by Tennessee Williams, adapted to film for the first time by Irving Rapper in 1950. In the story, one of the characters has a collection of little glass animals, from which one (a unicorn) is knocked to the floor, breaking off its horn.; During the production of the Amazon Fury Part I DLC, a Broadway revival of the play was running in the Booth Theatre. It was nominated to 7 categories at the Tony Awards, winning the award for the Best Lighting Design of a Play.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: When you first get into the instance, you must first speak to Nightwing. He will tell you to head to the training simulator room. After you head there, Starfire and Beast Boy will test you with a series of holographic enemies. You fight alongside Robin and Terra as allies, but after you beat all Holograms, Terra goads Robin into fighting you himself. Starfire says that it's not necessary, but Robin uses the terminal to lock Starfire and Beast Boy in the control room. This is where you will fight Robin. After you reduce his health, he stops attacking and says that he merely wanted to evaluate if you were worthy to be a Titan. But all of a sudden, the Hologram system goes haywire, and you will have to defeat a series of holograms based off of Giganta , Major Force , Monsieur Mallah , and Queen Bee . And after you beat all those, the simulator decides to load a level 9000 threat: Holographic Trigon . Defeat the hologram to finish the instance. During the battle, he will summon holograms of possessed heroes. After you defeat the hologram, Cyborg blows down the entrance and says that the tower systems are going haywire and he needs all hands on deck. And that's the end of the duo.

title: War Crimes
summary: War Crimes is a Tier 8 4-player operation in Age of Justice released in May 2017.

sections.title: Overview
items: War Crimes is a Tier 8 4-player operation in Age of Justice released in May 2017.
Access to the War Crimes operation requires a combat rating of 150.

Baron Von Savage's troops are raiding the future to steal modern technology and resources to bring back to World War II. Every bit of time-displaced technology causes more instability in the time stream. Stop as much future tech from traveling to the past as you can.

sections.title: Story
items: " Baron Von Savage's troops are taking anything that isn't nailed to the floor... Actually, they're taking that stuff too. Every piece of tech they steal from the modern era has disastrous repercussions for the time stream when brought to the past. You need to shut down their time portals and recover anything they've stolen until we can fix the past." — Rip Hunter
" Oh, Rip, no need to be quite so melodramatic. If I've learned anything in my millenia on this Earth it's that time is relative..." — Vandal Savage

Per Degaton and stormtroopers are raiding the future to steal modern technology and resources. Follow a lead to the Sentinels of Magic citadel, but be careful. Something seems fishy about this particular jaunt to the future. They’re after anything that can give them an advantage in World War II.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Rip Hunter and Vandal Savage are in a truce working together attempting to stop Per Degaton and his theft of future weaponry. After defeating a few rooms of mobs and closing portals in a warehouse (which coincidentally looks a lot like Monarch Playing Card Company), you catch up to Degaton, who escapes and leaves Savage Captain Merzen to deal with you.

He would summon more and more Savage Infantry and Savage Grenadiers, but they are immobile, assembled starting from the east and west edge of the room, and closing in towards the middle as the battle progresses. The Infantry strafes north-south and will damage and push you back if you get in the line of fire.

Track Per Degaton to the Sentinels of Magic Citadel, where "Doctor Fate" claims you will not steal the Spear of Destiny and attacks you. Upon defeat, the real Doctor Fate appears, revealing your opponent to be Eclipso, who escapes. Humorously, Doctor Fate states it should be obvious that was not him, as he is not one to "spout empty cliches" (despite them being perfectly in line with his normal dialogue), and it is implied the players characters looked at him incredulously for that comment.
Player characters who get the purple pulse in the final fight against Eclipso can cleanse themselves by passing through one of the ankhs Doctor Fate spawns in the room.

title: Zetta-Drone
summary: The Zetta-Drone is a large Security Sentry designed to fend off invaders within the Batcave: Inner Sanctum.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Zetta-Drone is a large Security Sentry designed to fend off invaders within the Batcave: Inner Sanctum.
Corrupted by Brainiac, the Zetta-Drone is the second boss encountered in the Batcave: Inner Sanctum raid/alert.

sections.title: Involvement
items: Brother Eye and Brainiac have taken over the Batcave's mainframe and, along with it, the substantial automated defense and security forces. Both heroes and villains battle against Earth's real enemy.

sections.title: Combat Tips
items: The Zetta-Drone is arguably the easiest boss in this instance. It is always accompanied by four smaller Bat-Drones which should be ignored for the most part as they will immediately be replaced when destroyed. However, this could be exploited with certain moves such as an Encasement- Pyrokinesis combo that allows you to do massive damage to the Zetta-Drone as long as it is near the Bat-Drones.

OMAC Nano Repair Units will periodically spawn at either the North or South side of the room. They are slow-moving green Omacs that are highly susceptible to crowd control effects and will self destruct once their health is low enough. For the most part they will ignore the players and attempt to get close to the Zetta-Drone and heal it, which is why they need to be destroyed quickly. Their healing move is vulnerable to interrupt.

As the fight progresses the boss will gain two different spin abilities. The first will be at around 80% health and will cause it to spin into the player team, knocking back and damaging everyone. The second spin acquired at around 40% health will cause it to move North and South in a straight line down the middle of the room. Players should stay out of its path and focus on the drones.
It will also sometimes "upgrade" one of the Bat Drones, causing it to spin uncontrollably into the player team until it is destroyed.

title: Brother Eye (Batcave: Inner Sanctum)
summary: Brother Eye is fought as the final boss of the Batcave: Inner Sanctum alert and raid.

sections.title: Overview
items: Brother Eye is fought as the final boss of the Batcave: Inner Sanctum alert and raid.

The fight consists of two distinct phases. During the first phase, Brother Eye is untargetable, but will continuously damage any players in laser fields on the floor, while summoning hordes of drones. Once in a while he would use a special attack.
Pulsar sequence - red pulsing fields that damages and knocks back players.
Gravity sequence - yellow and black fields and pulls and slows players.

Laser sequence - by far the most lethal attack. Massive lasers, two at a time, slash across the entirety of the boss room multiple times, leaving scorching trails. Easily hits over 1000 (possibly twice) and knocks back players.

After taking down all five terminals on the wall with Batman's help, Brother Eye detaches from the wall and attacks on the battlefield. This phase can be easy or very hard. In this state Brother Eye has two attacks.
Brother Eye fires a laser that sweeps in a 360-degrees manner around the whole room. However, this hits mid air so any player on the ground can ignore this.
Brother Eye spins rapidly while moving, inflicting extreme melee damage and knocking back players, easily killing any player of the relevant level in one combo.
Additionally, Brother Eye can teleport to any point within the boss room.

The key to this phase is avoiding the spin attack; as long as you do, he won't do any damage. His teleport has a long animation, so start dodging once you see it. His spin moves faster than you can, so you want to be a safe distance away before he starts spinning. While it could be very hard if the team is not experienced, some players can just kite almost indefinitely and solo this phase with sufficient practice, even without being overgeared.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: The whole raid is structured into four phases.
The raid group should have at least one Healer and one Controller. A Tank is not a must, but can be helpful in phase three.
It is advisable to bring Qwa-Bombs and Exobyte Interference Shields into the raid, since those will speed up the completion time considerably.
It is possible to complete this raid in five minutes counted from the time the players enter the fighting area.
Phase 1

In phase 1 nine anti-matter shards will appear. Those must be destroyed. Qwa-Bombs help a lot here since each bomb takes away 40% of the current health of the shards. With four to five bombs a shard can be destroyed pretty quickly. The next shard will always appear when the current shard is down to about 30%-40% (?) health.

Adds can pretty much be ignored as they surround the shards and will go down as a side effect from attacking the shards. All players should always attack the shards. If the group is good enough, splitting into smaller groups can further speed up things.
Phase 2

Attack the Anti-Monitor. The boss is in the center of the map and has some pink AOE areas around him. Avoid those areas as you will be levitated into the air and lose valuable time. It is advisable to use Exobyte Interference Shields when players are surrounded with small black anti-matter spheres to avoid additional anti-matter effects like being pushed around etc.
When the Anti-Monitor has lost about two third of his health phase three starts.
Phase 3

Shadow Demons and Shadowlings will start to appear all around the Anti-Monitor from spawn points indicated by small black anti-matter spheres. Everytime one of those dark creatures reaches the Anti-Monitor, he will grow stronger. The goal is to defeat 20 of those black shadow creatures.

A good strategy is to form a circle around the Anti-Monitor. The shadow creatures will stop walking towards the Anti-Monitor after a bit of damage-in. Qwa-Bombs will work fine here, but crowd control effects will also work. Avoid the pink AOE areas the boss does lay out and ignore all other adds which still might be around.
After 20 Shadow Demons or Shadowlings have been defeated, the final phase begins.
Phase 4
Attack the Anti-Monitor again. This time he can be defeated and the raid ends with the Anti-Monitor giving a short speech.

sections.title: Overview
items: Kaznia Crown

Day of Reckoning is Tier 7 playable content that contains the open world Kaznia City, the raid DoR: Kaznian Necropolis Onslaught and a scaled-down alert version DoR: Kaznian Necropolis Assault, the challenge DoR: Desecrated Mausoleum, and a Flashback version of the raid DoR: Flashback: Neron's Underworld originally from The Sins of Black Adam.
The chapter is intended to be the first of a 4-part Story Arc, " Light and Rain".
The Casual mode version is available for player characters with level 20 or above.
This chapter also features an event running from January 28 through February 24, 2025, where exclusive rewards and resources can be earned by completing missions to earn progress points.
Chapter 1: Day of Reckoning was released on January 28th, 2025. Access to this content is available to all players for free.

sections.title: Story
items: " Alright, mate? Look, I could use your help - there's a killer on the loose. I lost their trail in Gotham during that alien invasion rubbish, but I think they've relocated to Kaznia City. Meet me there at a nice little pub called the Laughing Hound. We've got work to do." — John Constantine

Uncover the truth that sleeps within Kaznia City, where a string of mysterious murders sends shockwaves through the streets. Teaming up with occult detective John Constantine of Justice League Dark, you’re caught in a web of supernatural secrets and discoveries that will challenge everything you know.
As the investigations progress, trust becomes a deadly gamble. Who can you rely on, and how many lives can you save before time runs out?
Brace yourself for some of the most horrifying discoveries to be made. Are you brave enough to face the cold-hearted truth of reality?

sections.title: Trivia
items: To access this content player characters must have completed either the mission Reap What You Sow (heroes) or Faustian Response (villains).
Teasers to Day of Reckoning can be found in the last episode, Harley Quinn vs. Apokolips, in the form of The Exobyte Killer (Briefings).
Story Blogs #1 to #3 serve as a prelude to Day of Reckoning.
Unlike previous episodes, Day of Reckoning was not put on the Test Server prior to official release.

Al Rivera, creative director for DC Universe™ Online wore a Blue Lantern ring and recited part of the oath at the end of the behind the scenes video. An in-game character with a blue ring is later shown at the launch trailer for the chapter, revealed to be Esperanza Cavalera on launch.

A log-in pop-up appeared before the proper launch, erroneously claiming that it only has a Solo and a Raid prior to its launch. It also advertised a "Lost Sinner Time Capsule", when it is revealed to be the Mystical Magician Time Capsule on launch.
Origin Augments are now maxed out at 412.
Generic gear's maximum level is raised to 395, although there is a bug with weapon boxes where the max level is displayed as 390. However, upon opening them, the actual max level is also 395.

Day of Reckoning's narrative is unusual in that the introductory mission series does not require queuing for instances, instead adapting an alert/raid for single player, followed by a more story-heavy version of the challenge instance. Said alert/raid ( DoR: Kaznian Necropolis Assault and DoR: Kaznian Necropolis Onslaught) are also unusual as slightly different versions of the same instance.

The Day of Reckoning update changed "Story" difficulty to "Casual". It is possibly due to Reckoning's Hideout and Kaznian Necropolis Strike being story-heavier versions of On Duty instances, and to avoid confusion.

sections.title: Story
items: From the depths of sorrow, a spark of hope ignites. In Chapter Four of Light and Rain: Hope Burns Bright, the Gray energy wave continues to spread across the stars, threatening to extinguish all life. Mogo, once mournful, now stands on the brink of becoming something far worse, frozen, shattered, and lost forever. Luzia Cavalera’s sorrow has reached a critical point, and unless she is reached in time, the living planet will not survive.
Stand with the Lantern Corps as hope and will clash against rage and despair. The future of Mogo and the emotional spectrum itself depends on you.

sections.title: Story
items: The battle against fear takes a darker turn in Chapter Three of Light and Rain: Raging Night. Plunging players into the heart of despair as sorrow, death, and corruption threaten to consume the living planet Mogo. Lyssa Drak has unleashed Nekron and the Black Lanterns, using Luzia Cavalera’s transformation into a Gray Lantern to spread sorrow energy that drains and weakens Lanterns. With sorrow spreading unchecked, you must stand alongside Kyle Rayner to save as many as possible before it’s too late.

sections.title: Mournful Mogo
items: Mogo has become a world shrouded in grief, transformed into a Gray Lantern by the sorrow energy radiating from Luzia. As Nekron’s forces close in, Heroes and Villains will meet Kyle Rayner on the planet’s surface to mount a desperate defense.

sections.title: RN: Book of the Black / RN: Book of the Black Alert
items: Deep within a dark cave on Mogo, the Book of the Black stirs. Drawn into its pages, you discover Lyssa Drak’s schemes, her prisoners bound, and Luzia’s sorrow twisted to serve a darker purpose. Whispers of Sinestro, Larfleeze, and the shadow of Nekron linger in the void, hinting at betrayals and a fate that pushes Luzia toward despair.

sections.title: RN: Nekron's Lair
items: The final confrontation draws near. Nekron, Lord of the Unliving, has risen, and only the light of a White Lantern can oppose him. In this new solo instance, Heroes and Villains must journey into Nekron’s Lair, recover Atrocitus, and forge a White Lantern to challenge the embodiment of death itself.

sections.title: RN Flashback: Corrupted Zamaron
items: "The Black" has re-emerged in the universe and has targeted the Predator entity inside the Central Power Battery on Zamaron. Help Carol Ferris defend Zamaron from the Black Lanterns!

sections.title: RN Flashback: Blackest Night
items: A massive Black Lantern has erupted from the blood-soaked streets of war-torn Metropolis and Nekron has risen from this deathly soil. You must fight alongside Carol Ferris and the Lantern Corps and send Nekron back to the Land of the Unliving.

title: Mechanic
summary: Mechanic in a video game is referring to a fixed course of action, which needs to be taken to properly advance in a specific game situation.

sections.title: Overview
items: Mechanic in a video game is referring to a fixed course of action, which needs to be taken to properly advance in a specific game situation.

The term is mostly used for non-obvious (re)actions, which need to be learned in order to advance, but by definition includes any such action. E.g. having to block a skull attack is a very obvious game mechanic, while an example for a more complex mechanic would be avoiding the Cyberadication while fighting Brainiac in the Brainiac: The Command Ship raid:
Periodically Brainiac will teleport to the middle of the room at approximately 25/50/75% health and generate a shield, while preparing a powerful attack and having an orange icon above his head.
There will be three terminals in the room that players will need to activate quickly to remove the shield, and then a player will need to lunge Brainiac to counter him.

If Brainiac isn't interrupted in time (approximately 10 seconds from when his shield goes up) he will unleash a powerful shockwave (Cyberadication) to the group. In the normal version of the raid this will deal large damage, however in the elite version this will likely cause a group wipe.
Especially raids may feature more complex mechanics. However many of those are hinted by on-screen texts or audio tells, so players would be able to prepare and react properly if paying attention.
In elite and elite plus instances, failing mechanics is almost always lethal. On the other hand instances can be finished even by average players by properly following the required mechanics.

Ninja looting is the term used for a player that needs gear and plans that aren't asigned to their role. If a Tank "needs" an armour piece or an R&D plan (eg.Vitalization & Power V) that is required for a Controller the Tank is then classified as a ninja due to the fact that the armour and plan have no benefit for the tank in combat. It is highly unacceptable to ninja, especially in a hard raid or alert unless the instance has explicitly been titled as style run by its players.

sections.title: First boss: Cursed Wonder Girl
items: Cursed Wonder Girl uses Hand Blast.

Lightning Bolt: She conjures lightning orbs under her targets, which detonate after a delay (looks like Word of Power) dealing damage in an area. You can be hit by multiple detonations but you can also move away from the balls to not be hit.
Voltaic Blast: A faster lightning blast (looks like a white Word of Power) damaging all targets.
Static Discharge: She damages and stuns all targets.
Static Push: An arc of energy bursts forward from her, knocking back targets in its path.
Spark Barrage: She shoots 5 sparks in a narrow arc, each dealing damage if it hits.
Electric Overload: Stuns and continuously damages a single target. Looks very similar to Pulse Beam and can also be interrupted.

She has 3 lethal attacks warned with the skull icon. They all have feats associated with avoiding/blocking them. Zatanna's attacks can interrupt them, so you may need to wait for Wonder Girl to use it a few times. Only 1 is available to Wonder Girl at a time, depending on her health percentage.

Ball Lightning: Zatanna says "Avoid the ball lightning!" Wonder Girl releases a slow-moving barrage of ball lightning expending from her in a circle, damaging on contact. Players can fly or climb walls above it, or dodge through them. She only uses it at high health (~70%+).
Ground Smash: Red cracks appear on the ground beneath her, before she jumps and smash down on the same spot. If blocked, it does no damage. She only uses it at medium health (about 30% to 60%).
Lunge Tackle: Wonder Girl shouts "Incoming!" and leaps at the player to damage them, vulnerable to block. She only uses it at low health (under ~30%).

sections.title: Second boss: Cursed Zatanna
items: Cursed Zatanna uses Hand Blast and Sorcery abilities, including Condemn, Soul Bolt, Karmic Backlash, and Karmic Suspension, with her Soul Barrage being able to hit quite hard.
Cursed Glitter Ball: Zatanna fires a cluster of glittery silver balls that stuns and damages on contact. Warned with Lethal attack icon.

Similar to Wonder Girl, Zatanna has 2 lethal attacks warned with the skull icon, both with feats associated with avoiding/blocking them. Only 1 is available to Zatanna at a time, depending on her health percentage.

Magical Orbital: Zatanna stomps the ground, electric beams appear from outside the boss area, aimed at the ground below her targets. After a delay, they damage and stun targets standing on them (although you can only be hit once). She only uses it at high health (above ~30%).

Aerial Blaster: Zatanna may summon 2 lilac orbs of energy, and after their own skull warning, fire beams that deal heavy damage. Despite Wonder Girl's advice, it doesn't seem possible to dodge those beams - rather, if blocked, they deal no damage. She only uses it at low health (under ~30%).

title: SoBA: The Treachery of Black Adam
summary: SoBA: The Treachery of Black Adam is a tier 6 solo challenge in the The Sins of Black Adam episode. It also features an elite version.

sections.title: Overview
items: Coin of Ra
SoBA: The Treachery of Black Adam is a tier 6 solo challenge in the The Sins of Black Adam episode. It also features an elite version.
Combat Rating: 368
Event version: Level 12+

sections.title: Story
items: Billy Batson's News Recap! Black Adam traveled to Neron's Underworld to rescue his beloved Isis! But, did it work? Tune in to find out!

sections.title: Characters
items: Black Adam
Greed
Neron
Billy Batson
Isis

sections.title: Locations
items: Underworld

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: After fighting through Lesser Demons and Skeletons, you enter a chamber and confront Neron who stands on a higher floor. He informs you that you have awakened Greed, which then appears on the ground.

sections.title: First boss: Greed
items: Greed attacks with Hand Blast. He has two special mechanics:
He can remove all your abilities and replaces your weapon with Brawling (interact with the treasure chest in the southwest corner to undo this).

Gold Crush: At 75%, 50%, and 25% health, Greed teleports to the center of the room and become immune to damage. You must destroy at least 3 of the 6 piles of treasures around the room to interrupt this or he will do massive damage to all targets. If he succeeds in using Gold Crush, he can immediately follow up with another Gold Crush or ability disable, so it is vital to interrupt.

After defeating him, continue until you find Neron at the final chamber of the underworld castle. Black Adam attempts to trade the player's soul for Isis, but Neron finds them unworthy (hero) or says they will belong to him anyway (villain) and instead asks for Kahndaq, saying he will split Isis into deadly and virtuous halves, one for the living and one for the underworld. Black Adam accepts, but was tricked when Neron traps the virtuous Isis in the underworld and releases the deadly one.

sections.title: Last boss: Neron
items: Neron also attacks with Hand Blast. He has two special mechanics:

Pool of Lava: Multiple pools appear on the ground, dealing heavy continuous damage if you are within (ignores Shield Powers, but does not damage pets). Neron does not have a grounding attack - players with Flight can simply remain in the air to avoid this entirely (you need to Breakout quickly if Neron uses a knock down weapon combo like Meteor Blast though). Otherwise, you can stand in the raised rocks on the north side of the chamber (behind Isis) as lava pools can only appear on flat ground.

True Form: At 75%, 50%, and 25% health, Neron teleports to the east side of the chamber and splits into four. The true form is the one with green smoke around his legs. If it is not KO'ed in time, the illusions disappear and Neron stuns and deal heavy damage ( Shield Power can block the damage) to all nearby targets. Because he does not move during this time and this attack has a limited range, you can avoid this by standing on the west side, or hovering above near the ceiling on the east side. Do not stay in the air on the west side, because this can cause his health to reset. Therefore, staying high up in the air on the east side can negate both of his mechanics. While Neron is vulnerable to control effects, which can interrupt the True Form attack (before he can split into 4), he will keep attempting to use it, and if interrupted too many times, his health can also reset, which should be avoided.

items: Canned Heat: Defeat Neron while 4 lava fields are active in SoBA: The Treachery of Black Adam solo. (25 points)

sections.title: Trivia
items: Story-wise, this challenge is framed as a flashback (as Billy Batson is "recapping" it) of events occurring prior to Infernal Kahndaq.
Upon release, this was simply titled "The Treachery of Black Adam" without the prefix. This was soon fixed.

If you go up to Neron's upper floor, he can be attacked and damaged but this would cause him and Greed to continuously be reset back on that floor. This can be fixed by going back down to ground level to fight Greed normally.

In the upper-level library on the opposite wall where Neron is first spotted, a book on a table could be found, titled "Hex Appeal" and featuring Zatanna on the cover. This book is also available as base items: Hex Appeal and Hex Appeal - Stack.
Greed's treasure piles contain plush dolls of Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, Lex Luthor, Joker, and King Shark (albeit with a classical depiction, not the hammerhead version of King Shark in DCUO).
Greed's combat voice lines are recycled from James, appropriately Trigon's son of Greed.
Only the first half of the Underworld map is accessible in this instance. It would be fully explored in SoBA: Neron's Underworld.

Neron is briefly targetable before the cutscene prior to his boss fight. He will continue to take damage during the cutscene and could even fall below the 75% health threshold to trigger his first True Form attack.

There are a number of paintings in the instance:; There are two in a chamber under the stairs near the entrance.; The one in the east depicts the aurora over some hills.; The one in the west depicts a skeletal figure with glowing eyes.; There are five in a chamber west of where you fight Greed.; The one on the north side of the entrance corridor depicts a cloudscape.; The one on the east wall depicts a sunset/sunrise above water and boats.; The one on the south wall depicts two skeletal figures.; The one on the west wall (top) is a replica of Saturn Devouring His Son.; The one on the west wall (bottom) is a replica of The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.
